passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.permSign`. The alternating sign fixes the curl convention in cylindrical component arrays. Repeated indices contribute zero; the order of the two gradient indices matters.

comparisons.note: The alternating symbol is +1 on cyclic permutations, −1 on anticyclic permutations, and zero when an index repeats. These signs fix the orientation of the curl.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.pinField`. Turns the stored polynomial constraint coefficients into the period-one matrix field Ξᵢ. The action on a perturbation is defined elsewhere.

comparisons.note: The pinning tensor Ξᵢ is obtained by evaluating its cell-polynomial matrix coefficients with the chosen symmetry order. Its pairing with a perturbation is defined separately.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.labelDensity`. Evaluates the full mode form using the parameter's period, weights and bounds at time zero and angle zero. It is the reduced Iι density, before multiplication by r.

comparisons.note: The reduced mode density uses the parameter's period, weights, and harmonic bounds at normalized time zero and angle zero. The cylindrical factor r is inserted when integrating it.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.stretchPosMean`. Averages the positive part of the stretching expression over time and angle. Taking the positive part before averaging differs from taking the positive part of the averaged expression.

comparisons.note: The expression first takes the positive part of the stretching density and then averages over one time period and all azimuthal angles. The order of these operations is retained.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.formPos`. Adds the sum of positive mode-density integrals and the mean positive stretching integral, with cylindrical weight r. Its value lies in the extended nonnegative reals and can be infinite.

comparisons.note: The positive reduced integral sums the nonnegative mode contributions and the averaged positive stretching contribution over the quarter-plane with weight r. Finiteness requires a separate estimate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsModeClass`. Requires positive azimuthal order and membership of the half-time rotation and spatial flip in Γ. This predicate alone does not say that every element of Γ is generated by them.

comparisons.note: The symmetry set contains the rotation by π/κ with a half-period time shift and the spatial flip with no time shift. These requirements give κ≥1 and do not require the whole symmetry set to be generated by these elements.

passages.quote: The symmetry order satisfies κ≥1.

comparisons.note: The symmetry order satisfies κ≥1.

passages.quote: Γ contains rotation by π/κ combined with a half-period time shift.

comparisons.note: Γ contains rotation by π/κ combined with a half-period time shift.

passages.quote: Γ contains the spatial flip with zero time shift.

comparisons.note: Γ contains the spatial flip with zero time shift.

comparisons.note: The modal Dirichlet density is |∂ᵣφ|²+|∂zφ|²+k²|φ|²/r². A patch separated from the axis avoids the radial denominator singularity.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.realPartVec`. The coordinatewise real part is packaged as a real continuous linear map so that it can be composed with derivative maps.

comparisons.note: The operation takes the real part of each of the three complex components. It is linear over the real numbers and is continuous.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeHess`. Second-derivative maps of the individual harmonic terms are summed and passed through the real-part map.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertReduction.shiftGradCoeff`. The cubic branch uses half the gap coefficient because the form estimate combines ∇u and ∆u through the weighted energy inequality.

comparisons.note: The L³ contribution to the quadratic-form shift is 1/(√3√w_*), half its contribution to the profile gap; the alternative L² coefficient is c_w.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.cellIndex`. Counts internal knots at or below the evaluation point, so an interior knot selects the piece on its right. Values outside the chart range are still defined.

comparisons.note: The selected interval is determined by the number of internal knots at or below the coordinate. At an internal knot, the piece on the right is chosen.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.cellCount`. Uses list length minus one with natural-number subtraction. Mesh validity is needed to rule out malformed short lists.

comparisons.note: The interval count is the number of knots minus one, with result zero for an empty list. A valid mesh has enough ordered endpoints to represent actual intervals.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline`. A spline supplies a polynomial for every pair of natural indices. A finite serialisation must specify values outside the valid rectangle indices.

anchor.heading: Polynomial pieces on a tensor mesh (L1221)

comparisons.note: A spline specifies a complex bivariate polynomial for each pair of interval indices. Values beyond the active mesh range are also part of the representation.

passages.quote: The two knot lists selecting polynomial rectangles.

comparisons.note: The radial and height knot lists select the polynomial rectangles.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.evalHalf`. Evaluates the polynomial selected by the two knot lists. The definition contains no interpolation or continuity check; join predicates establish those properties.

comparisons.note: Evaluation first selects the radial and height intervals and then evaluates their polynomial at the given chart coordinates. Agreement and continuity across interfaces require the joining conditions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.atFirst`. Replaces the first polynomial variable by a complex constant while leaving the second variable unchanged.

comparisons.note: The operation substitutes a fixed complex value for the first polynomial variable and leaves the second variable unchanged.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.atSecond`. Replaces the second polynomial variable while preserving the first. This is used in exact polynomial join identities.

comparisons.note: The operation substitutes a fixed complex value for the second polynomial variable and leaves the first variable unchanged.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.tDeriv`. Iterates formal differentiation in the first variable. Order zero leaves the polynomial unchanged.

comparisons.note: The operator takes the specified number of polynomial derivatives in the radial chart variable. Order zero leaves the polynomial unchanged.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.xDeriv`. Iterates formal differentiation in the second variable, which represents the chart height rather than a Cartesian coordinate.

comparisons.note: The operator takes repeated polynomial derivatives in the normalized-height variable, with the radial variable fixed.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.conj`. Keeps the mesh and conjugates each polynomial coefficient. This is the coefficient-level operation used for harmonic reality conditions.

comparisons.note: Conjugation leaves the spline mesh unchanged and replaces every polynomial coefficient by its complex conjugate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.VanishesFrom`. Quantifies over all natural indices, using one as the default radial knot. Thus a cutoff below one also constrains out-of-range pieces, not only the serialised valid cells.

anchor.heading: Zero spline pieces after a cutoff (L1241)

comparisons.note: Every polynomial whose radial left knot is at or beyond the cutoff must vanish, including all height indices. Missing radial knots are assigned value 1, so a cutoff below 1 also requires the corresponding out-of-range pieces to vanish.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.weightPoly`. Forms σ^e₀(1−σ)^e₁, the origin and infinity factors used in the field formulas. The exponents are natural numbers.

comparisons.note: The endpoint weight is σ^e₀(1−σ)^e₁ for nonnegative integers e₀ and e₁. These powers control the origin and far-field behavior.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.radialScale`. Applies σ(1−σ)∂σ, corresponding to |y|∂|y| in (B.3). Radial phase terms are added by later operators.

comparisons.note: The radial scaling operator is σ(1−σ)∂σ, which equals |y|∂|y| under the compactification. Oscillatory radial phases contribute separate terms.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.heightDeriv`. Differentiates the chart coefficient in η while fixing σ. This is separate from the physical height derivative in cylindrical coordinates.

comparisons.note: The chart derivative is ∂η at fixed compactified radius σ. It differs from differentiating with respect to the physical height z.

comparisons.note: The interior polynomial is [(x−a)(b−x)]^n[x−(a+b)/2]^s. Its endpoint derivatives of orders 0 through n−1 vanish at both ends.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.dofPoly`. A coordinate contributes only to its adjacent nodal interval or its own bubble interval, and out-of-range derivative or bubble orders contribute zero.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.dofSign`. The reflection sign is (−1)^p for a pth derivative and (−1)^s for a midpoint bubble of order s.

comparisons.note: A reflected p-th endpoint derivative has sign (−1)^p, and a reflected midpoint polynomial of degree s has sign (−1)^s.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetAxis`. Strict knot order, the specified endpoints and positive depth are required. Nonzero gaps follow on active intervals from these conditions.

comparisons.note: The reference field must equal the converted harmonic representation, with the Hessian set to zero on the chosen seams. Each forcing field has its own admissible compact representation, and the declared reference harmonic set may contain unused modes.

comparisons.note: The scaled representative data satisfy coefficient and scale-symmetry conditions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasEdgeBreak`. Requires the chosen support boundary to occur in both amplitudes used by each field key, choosing the nonzero-azimuthal or axisymmetric representation as appropriate.

anchor.heading: Support boundary is a spline knot (L4828)

comparisons.note: For every active harmonic, the support boundary must be a breakpoint of both amplitude splines used in its angular case.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime`. Maps the lattice label ι to 2ι₂−ι₁, the integer multiplying 2π times the period-one time variable in (B.2).

comparisons.note: The temporal integer associated with ι is 2ι₂−ι₁. It multiplies 2π times the normalized time in (B.2).

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth`. Maps ι to κι₁, the integer multiplying the spatial angle in (B.2).

comparisons.note: The angular integer associated with ι is κι₁, as in (B.2).

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.labelHarmonic`. Combines the temporal and azimuthal integers for use with the imported mode operators. It preserves the distinction between lattice labels and frequency pairs.

anchor.heading: Frequency pair of a lattice label (L1713)

comparisons.note: The lattice label ι corresponds to the temporal-angular frequency pair (2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁).

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip`. Implements ι↦(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁), which reverses the angular frequency and preserves the time frequency.

comparisons.note: Reflection sends ι to (−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁). It reverses the angular frequency and preserves the temporal frequency.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.flipLabel`. Reverses the second coordinate of a frequency pair. Its input is already a temporal-angular frequency pair, unlike labelFlip's lattice label.

comparisons.note: For a temporal-angular frequency pair (n,k), reflection gives (n,−k).

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.IsLatticeHarmonic`. Asserts that a frequency pair is the image of some lattice label. Injectivity of the label map needs a positive azimuthal order.

comparisons.note: An allowed frequency pair is one arising from a lattice label through (2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁). Positive κ ensures that this label is unique.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.planePoint`. Embeds a meridian point in space at angle zero, where the reduced mode densities are evaluated.

comparisons.note: The meridian point (r,z) is placed at (r,0,z), the spatial point of angle zero.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.labelVel`. Uses the frequency pair of ι and evaluates the mode at time zero and angle zero. This is a spatial component array of the mode in (B.12).

anchor.heading: Velocity mode on the meridian plane (L1723)

comparisons.note: The velocity coefficient uses the harmonic associated with ι and is evaluated at normalized time zero and angle zero. Its three entries are the cylindrical components on the meridian plane.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.labelGrad`. Reads the corresponding gradient mode as a pair-indexed complex array, retaining the order of output and derivative indices.

anchor.heading: Gradient mode on the meridian plane (L1726)

comparisons.note: The gradient coefficient is evaluated on the same time-zero, angle-zero meridian plane. Its two indices retain the gradient component convention used by the mode transform.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.flipPoint`. Implements rotation by π about the first Cartesian axis, sending (y₁,y₂,y₃) to (y₁,−y₂,−y₃).

comparisons.note: The symmetry sends (y₁,y₂,y₃) to (y₁,−y₂,−y₃), a rotation by π around the first coordinate axis.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.frameSign`. The radial component has sign +1 and the angular and axial components have sign −1 under the stored half-plane reflection.

comparisons.note: The reflected cylindrical components have signs +1, −1, −1 in the radial, azimuthal, and axial directions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.frameUnit`. Lists the radial, angular and axial vectors in component order. Matrix fields use the same order for both indices.

comparisons.note: The moving frame is ordered as (eᵣ,eφ,e_z). Vector and matrix components use this order.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.pointAngle`. Uses the complex argument of y₁+i y₂. Its branch convention is harmless only together with the periodic harmonic and axis regularity conditions.

comparisons.note: The angle is the argument of y₁+iy₂. Integer angular harmonics make the choice of argument branch consistent away from the axis, while axis regularity belongs to the complete field conditions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.pointPlane`. Returns (r,z), before the negative-height branch reflects z to the stored upper half-plane.

comparisons.note: The meridian coordinates of a spatial point are (√(y₁²+y₂²),y₃), retaining the sign of the height.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase`. Evaluates Eι from (B.2). The variable σ here denotes period-one time, unlike the paper's compactified radial σ in (B.3).

comparisons.note: The harmonic is Eι(θ,φ)=exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ]). Here θ is normalized time and φ is the spatial angle.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.labelValueAt`. For negative height, switches to labelFlip and multiplies by the supplied frame sign before evaluating at positive height. This is distinct from complex conjugation under label negation.

comparisons.note: At negative height, the coefficient is evaluated at reflected height using the reflected lattice label and the specified component sign. This operation preserves temporal frequency.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.planeValue`. Uses the component's reflection sign and the flipped label on negative height, while keeping upper-plane coefficients unchanged.

comparisons.note: The vector coefficient at negative height uses the reflected label with signs +1, −1, −1 for its three cylindrical components. At nonnegative height it uses the given polynomial directly.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.field`. Sums real harmonic contributions in the moving frame over every cell indicator. Shared cell boundaries may receive more than one contribution; the integral theory uses negligible overlaps.

comparisons.note: The field sums the real harmonic components in the cylindrical frame over the closed solid of every cell. Shared boundaries can receive multiple terms, while valid cell overlaps have zero measure.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.IsConjugateClosed`. Requires label closure under negation and flip and conjugate evaluated polynomials under negation. The polynomial equality quantifies over every label, not just labels in the finite set.

anchor.heading: Reality and reflection of vector data (L1820)

comparisons.note: Active vector harmonics are closed under negation and reflection. For every label, including labels outside the active set, the coefficient at −ι is the complex conjugate of the coefficient at ι.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.planeValue`. The reflection sign is the product of the two frame signs, reversing the entries with exactly one radial index.

comparisons.note: Matrix reflection multiplies an entry by the signs of both cylindrical indices. Exactly one radial index gives a minus sign.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.frameMap`. Maps column component b to row component a through frame vectors, giving a continuous linear map in Cartesian space. This fixes the gradient-index convention.

comparisons.note: The matrix acts by x↦∑ₐᵦMₐᵦ⟨eᵦ,x⟩eₐ. Thus its column index is the input direction and its row index is the output component.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.field`. Sums the real harmonic coefficient matrices after conversion to the moving frame, with a separate indicator for each cell solid.

comparisons.note: The matrix field sums the real harmonic matrices in the cylindrical frame on each closed cell solid. The same cell indicators are used as for the vector fields.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.IsConjugateClosed`. Requires finite labels closed under negation and flip, and conjugate polynomial values for every label and component pair. It does not by itself identify the matrix field as a derivative.

anchor.heading: Reality and reflection of matrix data (L1841)

comparisons.note: The active matrix labels are closed under negation and reflection, and opposite labels have conjugate component polynomials for every label. These conditions alone impose no derivative relation with a vector field.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.rowPartFactor`. Multiplication by −i makes the real part of a complex field equal its imaginary part. The true branch retains its real part.

comparisons.note: Multiplication by 1 preserves the real part, while multiplication by −i makes the real part equal the original imaginary part.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsActuatorInstance`. A single j_* rectangle contains each forcing-field label, and every label in that rectangle must avoid every λ- and μ-piece on K.

comparisons.note: The forcing labels lie in |ι₂|≤j_* and |ι₂−ι₁|≤j_*. For every α∈K, every label in that entire rectangle avoids every signed λ- and μ-piece mode set.

passages.quote: The cell certificate's azimuthal symmetry order κ is positive.

comparisons.note: The cell certificate's azimuthal symmetry order κ is positive.

passages.quote: Every stored forcing label lies in the j_* rectangle in ι₂ and ι₂−ι₁.

comparisons.note: Every stored forcing label lies in the j_* rectangle in ι₂ and ι₂−ι₁.

passages.quote: On K every label in that rectangle avoids every signed λ-piece mode set.

comparisons.note: On K every label in that rectangle avoids every signed λ-piece mode set.

passages.quote: On K every label in that rectangle avoids every signed μ-piece mode set.

comparisons.note: On K every label in that rectangle avoids every signed μ-piece mode set.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.GeneratedByClassSymmetries`. Each declared symmetry must be a nonnegative integral power of the half-period rotation, optionally followed by the spatial flip, with an additional integer time shift.

comparisons.note: Each declared symmetry has spatial action R_(aπ/κ)F^b and time shift a/2+j, with a a nonnegative integer, b either 0 or 1, and j an integer. Here F is the spatial flip.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey`. The key is the pair (ι,l) in Eι,l: its lattice label determines the time and azimuthal frequencies, while phaseIndex is the separate radial-phase integer.

comparisons.note: A harmonic is indexed by the pair (ι,l), where ι determines time and angular frequencies and l multiplies the radial phase f(|y|²).

passages.quote: Lattice label ι=(ι₁,ι₂) encoding the time and angular frequencies.

comparisons.note: The data specify the lattice label ι=(ι₁,ι₂) encoding the time and angular frequencies.

passages.quote: Integer l multiplying the radial phase f(\|y\|²).

comparisons.note: The data specify the integer l multiplying the radial phase f(|y|²).

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey.negKey`. Complex conjugation negates both the lattice label ι and the radial-phase integer l.

comparisons.note: Complex conjugation sends (ι,l) to (−ι,−l).

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey.flipKey`. The spatial flip maps ι to ι♭ and leaves l unchanged because the radial phase depends only on |y|².

comparisons.note: The spatial flip sends (ι,l) to (ι♭,l), preserving the radial-phase index because |y|² is unchanged.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyPhase`. Eι,l combines normalized time frequency 2ι₂−ι₁, azimuthal frequency κι₁ and radial phase l f(|y|²).

comparisons.note: The full phase is exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ+lf(|y|²)]), combining normalized time, angle, and radial oscillation.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyVector`. The three reduced components multiply y/|y|, p and a from (B.4), and the result is multiplied by Eι,l.

comparisons.note: One harmonic is its oscillatory factor times u₀y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a, with the chart amplitudes evaluated at σ and η.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.complexField`. The finite sum is formed before taking real parts, preserving the conjugate-pair construction of (B.6).

comparisons.note: The complex field is the finite sum of its active vector harmonics. The real part is taken after this sum.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoField`. The decoded real field is the real part of the finite complex harmonic sum, with normalized time as its first argument.

comparisons.note: The represented physical field is Re∑_(ι,l)Eι,l(u₀y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a), with normalized time as its time variable.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.harmonicsOf`. The image converts each stored lattice label to its actual time and azimuthal frequencies; radial-phase indices do not create additional time/angular labels.

comparisons.note: The physical time-angular support is the image of the active pairs under (ι,l)↦(2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁). The radial-phase index introduces no additional time or angular frequency.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.labelsOf`. The image forgets the radial-phase integer but retains the paper's lattice label ι. It is different from the physical-frequency image harmonicsOf.

comparisons.note: The lattice support retains each active ι and discards its radial-phase index l. It has yet to be converted to physical frequency pairs.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.orbitClosure`. The finite key set is enlarged by conjugation, reflection and their composition, retaining duplicates only once as a Finset.

comparisons.note: The completed key set contains the original pairs, their conjugates, their reflections, and their conjugate reflections. Repeated pairs occur only once.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.closureAmp`. The constructor prefers a directly stored representative, then its conjugate, then its reflection, then the combined transform. Representative uniqueness and fixed-orbit conditions make these choices consistent.

comparisons.note: The amplitude is taken from the supplied representative when available, otherwise from its conjugate, reflected, or conjugate-reflected representative in that order. Consistency requires the separate orbit and fixed-point conditions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.closureData`. The orbit-closed keys and their transformed amplitudes form the full TimeFieldData object used for evaluation.

comparisons.note: The complete harmonic field uses the symmetry-closed key set with amplitudes obtained by the corresponding conjugation and reflection operations.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.axisRotation`. The coordinate formula supplies the exact rotations under which each amplitude has one azimuthal wave number.

comparisons.note: Rotation through α acts on the first two Cartesian coordinates and fixes the vertical coordinate; these rotations determine the azimuthal transformation law of each amplitude.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.complexComponent`. Components 0 and 1 are R₁+iR₂ and R₁−iR₂; component 2 is R₃. These are scalar wave channels, not cylindrical vector components.

comparisons.note: The three scalar components are R₁+iR₂, R₁−iR₂ and R₃. The first two are circular combinations of Cartesian components.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.AdjointDefect.componentWeight`. The two circular components each receive weight 1/2 and the vertical component receives weight 1 in the squared norm.

comparisons.note: The circular components have squared-norm weight 1/2 each and the vertical component has weight 1, recovering the ordinary vector norm.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.gradAt`. The wrapper extracts the (a,b) cylindrical-frame entry of the label's gradient mode at a meridian point.

comparisons.note: This is the (a,b) component of the selected gradient harmonic in the cylindrical frame, evaluated at a meridian point.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.velAt`. The wrapper extracts one cylindrical-frame component of the label's vector mode at a meridian point.

comparisons.note: This is the selected cylindrical component of a velocity harmonic at the given meridian point.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellModelLong.IsLowLabel`. The test uses only |ι₁|≤cut, so it is an azimuthal label cutoff and does not bound the temporal index ι₂.

comparisons.note: A label is low when its first component satisfies |ι₁|≤N. The time-frequency component is unrestricted by this test.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.upperValue`. The upper table is selected at the compactified radius σ and the signed height ratio η; the radial decay factor is applied by eval.

comparisons.note: The upper table is read at the intervals containing σ and η. The decay factor is applied separately in the full spatial weight.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.lowerValue`. The lower table uses −η, so both half-space tables are indexed by a nonnegative height coordinate.

comparisons.note: The lower table is read at σ and −η, so the negative physical half-space uses a nonnegative chart-height coordinate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.eval`. The decoded weight is the selected table value times (1−σ) to an integer exponent; points on y₃=0 select the upper table.

comparisons.note: The spatial step weight is the selected half-table value times (1−σ)^h for an integer h. The upper table is used on the symmetry plane.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.mirror`. Reflection exchanges the upper and lower tables while retaining their common mesh and decay exponent.

comparisons.note: Reflection exchanges the two step tables and leaves their common knots and integer exponent unchanged.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsPositiveStep`. A valid tensor mesh is required independently of the positivity conditions on its active cells. Positivity concerns both half-space tables.

comparisons.note: The mesh must be valid, and every active entry of both step tables must be strictly positive.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.EpsGiven`. Lean calls the paper's λ-pieces eps-pieces; this record stores the scalar functions before the rotating frame and transport bound are supplied.

comparisons.note: A λ-piece supplies its harmonic set, scalar multiplier weight, and eight auxiliary step functions for error shares and balancing estimates. The rotation rate and transport bound are attached separately.

comparisons.note: The data specify the chart representation of the nonnegative multiplier weight λ_p.

comparisons.note: The data specify the step function allocating the first gradient/curl error share; positivity is required later.

comparisons.note: The data specify the local stretching length h, required positive by the compatibility conditions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.MuGiven`. The μ-piece stores one mode set, a decaying weight, two positive auxiliary step functions and a scalar for the Young bounds. Its eta field is that balancing constant, distinct from the height coordinate η.

comparisons.note: A μ-piece supplies its harmonic set, scalar weight, two auxiliary step functions, and a Young-inequality parameter. This scalar parameter is independent of the spatial chart coordinate η.

passages.quote: Physical time/azimuthal harmonic set N_p for this μ-piece.

comparisons.note: The data specify the physical time/azimuthal harmonic set N_p for this μ-piece.

passages.quote: Chart representation of the nonnegative multiplier weight μ_p.

comparisons.note: The data specify the chart representation of the nonnegative multiplier weight μ_p.

passages.quote: Step function allocating the transport-error share, required positive by the instance conditions.

comparisons.note: The data specify the step function allocating the transport-error share, required positive by the compatibility conditions.

passages.quote: Step function balancing the velocity coupling, required positive by the instance conditions.

comparisons.note: The data specify the step function balancing the velocity coupling, required positive by the compatibility conditions.

passages.quote: Scalar η in the μ-piece Young inequalities, required positive by IsWeightValues.

comparisons.note: The data specify the scalar η in the μ-piece Young inequalities, required positive by the scalar-weight conditions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.EpsGiven.mirror`. The mode set is mapped by the harmonic reflection, while all spatial scalar tables exchange their two half-spaces.

comparisons.note: Reflection reverses the angular frequency in the λ-piece mode set and exchanges the upper and lower charts of every associated scalar function.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.MuGiven.mirror`. Reflection acts on the mode set and scalar tables; the auxiliary number η is unchanged.

comparisons.note: Reflection reverses angular frequency and exchanges the μ-piece's half-charts, while retaining its scalar Young-inequality parameter.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues`. This record packages the class weights Dι and Zι together with the λ- and μ-pieces in their chart representation. Frame rates and transport bounds are attached later.

comparisons.note: The complete weight data combine the harmonic classes, the D and Z class weights, the λ- and μ-pieces, and the constants c and cμ. Rotation rates and transport bounds are supplied separately.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.epsPiece`. The constructor evaluates each stored scalar in the chart and adds the supplied rotation rate and transport-bound function.

comparisons.note: The λ-piece is obtained by evaluating its scalar and step-function data in the chart and adjoining the chosen rotation rate and transport majorant.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.muPiece`. The constructor evaluates the stored μ-weight and auxiliary steps while preserving its harmonic set and scalar η.

comparisons.note: The μ-piece evaluates its scalar weight and two step functions, retaining its harmonic set and Young-inequality parameter and adjoining the chosen frame and transport majorant.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.pieces`. The class map and constants are retained, while the scalar records become the function-valued PieceWeights used by the coercive form.

comparisons.note: The full multiplier family evaluates the D and Z class weights and every λ- and μ-piece, preserving the class assignment and constants c and cμ.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsWeightValues`. The record imposes the specified joining orders, origin behaviour, decay powers and positive auxiliary functions. Only the strain class weight Dι is required to be nonnegative here; Zι has different conditions.

comparisons.note: The weight conditions prescribe joining orders, behavior at the origin, decay powers, and positive auxiliary steps, with 0<c,cμ<1. Nonnegativity is required for D, λ, and μ; no such condition on Z appears here.

comparisons.note: There are finitely many multiplier coefficient classes.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.AdjointEntryLinks`. The record identifies the adjoint field, constant pin coefficients, moved centre/tangent fields and period rates. It also makes every fitted direction set empty on this route.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent`. Uses the x+iy, x−iy and axial components so that each has one azimuthal phase shift. This is the component encoding of the potential fields.

comparisons.note: The potential is represented by the circular components x+iy and x−iy and its vertical component, each with its own angular frequency shift.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent.shift`. Adds +1 for x+iy, −1 for x−iy, and zero for the axial component to the harmonic’s azimuthal frequency.

comparisons.note: The angular frequency is shifted by +1 for x+iy, by −1 for x−iy and by zero for the vertical component.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent.carriesSine`. The two horizontal complex components receive a polar-sine factor; the axial component does not.

comparisons.note: Both circular components receive the polar factor √(1−η²); the vertical component receives no extra sine factor.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotScalar`. A tensor-product Hermite amplitude is multiplied by explicit near-origin, far-field and axis factors. Endpoint vanishing may supply part of the required radial order.

comparisons.note: A scalar potential combines a tensor Hermite amplitude with explicit origin, infinity and axis factors. Vanishing endpoint derivatives can contribute additional radial order.

passages.quote: Tensor-product jet spline for the scalar amplitude.

comparisons.note: The scalar amplitude is specified by a tensor-product Hermite spline.

passages.quote: Explicit vanishing order at the compactified radial origin.

comparisons.note: The data specify explicit vanishing order at the compactified radial origin.

passages.quote: Explicit decay order at the compactified far endpoint.

comparisons.note: The data specify explicit decay order at the compactified far endpoint.

passages.quote: Power of 1−η² multiplying the amplitude near the polar axis.

comparisons.note: The data specify power of 1−η² multiplying the amplitude near the polar axis.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.polarSine`. Computes √(1−η²) using the height ratio defined on Cartesian points. Its values at the origin and axis follow the existing totalized chart conventions.

anchor.heading: Polar sine from the height ratio (L6741)

comparisons.note: The polar sine is √(1−η²), where η is the Cartesian height divided by the radius; its assigned value at the origin follows the chosen coordinate convention.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.scalarValue`. Combines time, azimuthal and radial phases with radial weights, axis factors and the spline value. The optional polar sine is separate from the integer axis power.

comparisons.note: The scalar harmonic combines its time, azimuthal and radial phases with radial powers, an axis factor and the spline value. A separate choice adds the polar sine.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.componentValue`. Supplies the component-specific azimuthal shift and polar-sine choice to the scalar potential decoder.

comparisons.note: Each circular or vertical component uses its corresponding angular frequency shift and polar-sine factor in the scalar harmonic formula.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.coordsOfComponents`. Recovers x and y from x+iy and x−iy using factors 1/2 and 1/(2i), while leaving the axial component unchanged.

comparisons.note: Cartesian components are recovered as (g₊+g₋)/2, (g₊−g₋)/(2i) and g_z.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotKeyData`. Stores amplitudes for G_j, U_j, the radial and polar contributions to F_j, and q_j. The radial/polar flux entries encode vector components of matrix columns.

comparisons.note: For each harmonic the amplitudes specify G, U, the radial and polar parts of the matrix potential F, and the scalar q.

passages.quote: Three complex-component amplitudes for G_j.

comparisons.note: The data specify three complex-component amplitudes for G_j.

passages.quote: Three complex-component amplitudes for U_j.

comparisons.note: The data specify three complex-component amplitudes for U_j.

passages.quote: Three component amplitudes multiplying the radial direction in F_j.

comparisons.note: The data specify three component amplitudes multiplying the radial direction in F_j.

passages.quote: Three component amplitudes multiplying the polar direction in F_j.

comparisons.note: The data specify three component amplitudes multiplying the polar direction in F_j.

passages.quote: Scalar amplitude for q_j.

comparisons.note: The data specify scalar amplitude for q_j.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotentialSeries`. Stores a finite key set and a total key-to-amplitude function. Only amplitudes at keys in the finite set enter the decoded field.

comparisons.note: Only the harmonics in the supplied finite set contribute to the potential, even though amplitudes can be specified for other harmonics as well.

passages.quote: Finite harmonic and phase keys included in the series.

comparisons.note: The data specify finite harmonic and phase keys included in the series.

passages.quote: Amplitude data for each possible key, read only on the selected keys.

comparisons.note: The data specify amplitude data for each possible key, read only on the selected keys.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.vectorPotential`. Sums the selected complex components, reconstructs Cartesian coordinates and takes the real vector. The selector chooses the G or U amplitude family.

anchor.heading: Decode G or U from its series (L6769)

comparisons.note: The chosen G or U components are summed over the finite harmonic set, converted to Cartesian coordinates and then replaced by their real parts.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxVector`. Forms a vector in the input index by combining the radial direction with the polar vector, for one output component and harmonic key.

comparisons.note: For one harmonic and output component, the flux combines the radial and polar direction vectors with their respective scalar amplitudes.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxEntry`. Sums the flux modes, reconstructs the output component and takes its real part. The two indices are output component a and input direction i.

anchor.heading: One entry of the potential flux (L6779)

comparisons.note: The flux entry is the real part of the summed harmonic contribution, with a denoting the output component and i the input direction.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxMap`. Turns the output-by-input matrix into a continuous linear map. Relative to the paper’s derivative convention this represents the transposed flux used in div F_jᵀ.

anchor.heading: Flux as a continuous linear map (L6783)

comparisons.note: The matrix acts on a vector by its output-by-input entries. This orientation gives the transposed matrix potential appearing in the paper's div Fᵀ convention.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.pressureValue`. Uses the unshifted harmonic azimuth, with no extra polar-sine factor, and takes the real part of the scalar sum.

comparisons.note: The scalar pressure sum uses the original azimuthal frequency without a component shift or extra sine factor, and its real part is retained.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotentialSeries.toPotentialData`. Packages the decoded G, U, flux and pressure functions into the adjoint-potential interface. This data conversion contains no proof of regularity.

anchor.heading: Bind series to four potential fields (L6789)

comparisons.note: The represented G, U, matrix potential and pressure are collected as four fields. Their analytic properties require the separate potential conditions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsJetMesh`. Requires strictly ordered breaks with specified endpoints. It intentionally omits the stronger joining conditions of IsJetAxis, allowing the tangential discontinuities permitted in the flux representation.

comparisons.note: The breakpoints must be strictly ordered with the prescribed first and last values. No matching of derivatives across intervals is required by this mesh condition alone.

passages.quote: The breakpoint list is strictly increasing.

comparisons.note: The breakpoint list is strictly increasing.

passages.quote: The first breakpoint is exactly the stated lower endpoint.

comparisons.note: The first breakpoint is exactly the stated lower endpoint.

passages.quote: The last breakpoint is exactly the stated upper endpoint.

comparisons.note: The last breakpoint is exactly the stated upper endpoint.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.StartVanishOrder`. Requires all node-jet coefficients below the requested order to vanish at the first radial breakpoint, for every polar degree of freedom.

anchor.heading: Zero radial jets at the origin (L6797)

comparisons.note: At the first radial breakpoint, all derivative coefficients below the specified order vanish for every angular coefficient.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.EndVanishOrder`. Requires the low-order radial node coefficients to vanish at the final compactified breakpoint, with the final index computed by cellCount.

comparisons.note: At the final compactified radial breakpoint, all derivative coefficients below the specified order vanish for every angular coefficient.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.dofMeetsEndCells`. Classifies node and bubble degrees of freedom that can affect the first or last cell. Natural subtraction in N−1 is truncated at zero.

anchor.heading: Degree of freedom touches an end (L6803)

comparisons.note: A coefficient touches an end cell when its node or bubble index lies in the stated first or last range; when N=0 the lower threshold N−1 is taken as zero.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.AxisCellsVanish`. Requires zero coefficients for every polar degree of freedom that touches either polar endpoint cell. This supplies an alternative to an explicit positive axis power.

comparisons.note: All angular coefficients affecting either endpoint cell must vanish. This can supply axis regularity in place of an explicit positive axis power.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.StartRowConstant`. Zeros all non-value polar degrees of freedom in the initial radial row and equates the remaining polar node values. This enforces one common scalar origin value.

anchor.heading: Constant angular row at the origin (L6810)

comparisons.note: The initial radial row has zero angular derivative and bubble coefficients, and every angular node value in that row is equal to one common constant.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialScalar`. Requires a first-order jet class in both variables. Near-origin and far-field orders may be supplied jointly by the explicit radial factor and vanishing endpoint jets.

comparisons.note: The amplitude has first-order joining in both variables, and its required origin and infinity orders may be split between explicit powers and vanishing endpoint derivatives.

passages.quote: The amplitude has jet regularity class (1,1).

comparisons.note: The amplitude and its first derivatives join in both spline variables.

passages.quote: A permitted initial jet-vanishing order combines with lowOrder to reach the required near-origin order.

comparisons.note: The explicit origin power and a permitted order of vanishing endpoint derivatives together reach the required origin order.

passages.quote: A permitted final jet-vanishing order combines with highOrder to reach the required decay order.

comparisons.note: The explicit infinity power and a permitted order of vanishing endpoint derivatives together reach the required decay order.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialSeries`. The G and U amplitudes have C¹ joining and the required decay; flux joining is required in its normal direction; pressure has separate axis and origin constraints. These are sufficient formal conditions for the analytic properties of (B.51), not a recovered file format.

comparisons.note: The vector potentials have the required first-order joining and radial decay, the matrix potential joins in its normal directions, and the pressure meets its separate axis and origin conditions. These are sufficient conditions for the analytic estimates of (B.51).

comparisons.note: Every G component has the scalar conditions with near-origin and decay orders at least two.

comparisons.note: Every U component has near-origin order at least two and decay order at least one.

comparisons.note: Both flux amplitude families achieve decay order at least two through explicit factors and endpoint vanishing.

comparisons.note: Each pressure amplitude is continuous across both families of spline seams.

passages.quote: Every pressure amplitude achieves decay order at least two.

comparisons.note: Every pressure amplitude achieves decay order at least two.

comparisons.note: Non-axisymmetric pressure has an axis factor and vanishes sufficiently at the radial origin.

comparisons.note: Axisymmetric pressure either has positive radial order or a constant polar row at the origin.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.Finite.quadValue`. Evaluates the real matrix form on a real vector. Symmetry and positivity are separate requirements, so this evaluator alone supplies neither.

comparisons.note: The value is xᵀMx for a real matrix M and a real vector x. Symmetry and nonnegativity require additional hypotheses on M.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.curlComp`. The component formula reads the gradient entry with output index first and derivative index second. That convention must be kept when comparing the paper's printed curl array.

comparisons.note: The curl component is the contraction ∑ⱼₗ εᵢⱼₗ sₗⱼ. Thus the first index of s is the vector component and the second is the differentiation direction.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBases`. Stores coefficient functions for every natural degree in r and z. A finite file therefore needs a specified continuation beyond the degrees it stores.

comparisons.note: The data give real monomial coefficients for radial and height polynomials at every nonnegative degree. A finite representation must specify how these coefficient families continue beyond its stored range.

passages.quote: Coefficient of each monomial in every radial basis polynomial.

comparisons.note: The data specify the coefficient of each monomial in every radial basis polynomial.

passages.quote: Coefficient of each monomial in every height basis polynomial.

comparisons.note: The data specify the coefficient of each monomial in every height basis polynomial.

passages.quote: The radial polynomial is ∑ᵢ₌₀ʲ aⱼᵢrⁱ, so its degree is at most j. The separate positive-leading-coefficient condition makes the degree exactly j.

comparisons.note: The formula uses coefficients through degree j and permits a zero leading coefficient, so the polynomial has degree at most j. Exact degree j requires the separate positive-leading-coefficient condition.

passages.quote: The height polynomial is ∑ᵢ₌₀ˡ bₗᵢzⁱ. Orthonormality and the positive leading coefficient are separate requirements on the family.

comparisons.note: The coefficient sum has degree at most l because its leading coefficient may vanish. Exact degree l and orthonormality follow from the separate conditions on the basis family.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBases`. The radial basis is orthonormal with lineWeight and the height basis with ordinary measure, with positive leading coefficients at every degree. These requirements fix normalisation and signs beyond the truncated cell unknowns.

comparisons.note: Both polynomial families have positive leading coefficients at every degree. Their inner products are Kronecker deltas, using the axis-dependent radial measure and ordinary height measure.

comparisons.note: All radial polynomials are orthonormal with the axis-dependent radial polynomial weight.

passages.quote: All height polynomials are orthonormal in ordinary interval measure.

comparisons.note: All height polynomials are orthonormal in ordinary interval measure.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.radialEigen`. Uses j(j+2) on axis cells and j(j+1) off the axis, with the square of the inverse half-width. Degree zero has eigenvalue zero.

comparisons.note: The radial eigenvalue is j(j+2)[2/(r₂−r₁)]² on axis cells and j(j+1)[2/(r₂−r₁)]² off the axis. Both give zero at j=0.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.heightEigen`. Uses the Legendre eigenvalue l(l+1) with the square of the inverse half-height. The degree-zero value is deliberately zero.

comparisons.note: The height eigenvalue is l(l+1)[2/(z₂−z₁)]². In particular, the constant height polynomial has eigenvalue zero.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.sumSq`. Adds squared complex moduli of all nine gradient entries, with no symmetry reduction.

comparisons.note: The gradient square is ∑ₐᵦ|sₐᵦ|² over all nine complex entries.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.vecSq`. Adds squared complex moduli of the three velocity components.

comparisons.note: The vector square is |v₁|²+|v₂|²+|v₃|².

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.curlSq`. Forms curlComp first, then sums the three squared moduli; it is not a sum over all nine entries.

comparisons.note: The curl square is the sum of the three squared moduli after antisymmetric contraction of the gradient. The three curl components determine this quantity.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.pairVec`. Packs nine gradient entries in row-major order 3a+b, then the three velocity entries. This fixes the coordinates of the 12 by 12 matrices in (B.26).

comparisons.note: The 12 coordinates list the nine gradient components in row order, followed by the three velocity components. This fixes the ordering in the local matrices of (B.26).

comparisons.note: The data specify polynomial cutoffs, resolved angular modes, the local 12×12 form, and the losses assigned to unresolved terms. In the time-periodic construction the corresponding choices are made for each space-time harmonic.

comparisons.note: The data specify the pointwise 12 by 12 complex matrix on gradient and velocity coordinates.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellScalars.rHat`. Divides cylindrical measure r by the basis weight. On an axis cell this agrees with one away from the axis; at r=0 Lean's total division gives zero.

comparisons.note: The measure ratio is r divided by the radial polynomial weight. It equals 1 for r>0 on an axis cell and takes the prescribed value 0 at r=0; the endpoint does not change integrals with respect to area measure.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.ParamData`. Stores selected relation rows, the unknown solved by each row, and retained skeleton unknowns. It does not itself assert that the solved block is invertible.

comparisons.note: The elimination data specify the relation matrix, one coordinate to solve for in each selected row, and retained boundary coordinates. Invertibility of the solved block is a separate requirement.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.quadFormValue`. Uses the conjugate of the first vector in the complex matrix pairing and returns its real part. Hermitian symmetry is a separate condition.

anchor.heading: Real part of a complex form (L453)

comparisons.note: The quadratic value is Re(u*Φu), with conjugation on the first vector. A Hermitian matrix is an additional assumption when that property is needed.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.edgeSign`. Chooses the sign from the relative order of the face and opposite-face coordinates. Equality is excluded separately by the face-validity predicate.

comparisons.note: The face orientation is +1 when the opposite coordinate is smaller and −1 otherwise. Valid face geometry ensures that the two coordinates differ.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.radialStripMoment`. Expresses a trace moment by an integral over the strip between a face and its opposite. The denominator is the signed face separation, and the final test polynomial depends on height.

comparisons.note: The radial trace moment is represented by a strip integral of F/(c−o)+(r−o)∂ᵣF/(c−o), with the orientation sign and the height test. The width c−o must be nonzero for the trace interpretation.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.heightStripMoment`. The corresponding strip integral differentiates in height and retains a supplied radial weight. Face orientation and the radial measure are independent choices.

comparisons.note: The height-strip formula uses F/(c−o)+(z−o)(∂F/∂z)/(c−o), multiplied by a radial test and its supplied radial weight. Its sign specifies the orientation of the two height faces.

comparisons.note: A side segment specifies its direction, trace and opposite coordinates, tangential interval, and polynomial tests. The opposite coordinate determines the strip used to recover the trace.

passages.quote: Selects a constant-radius face when true and a constant-height face when false.

comparisons.note: The face is selected as either constant-radius or constant-height.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.FaceSegment.test`. Evaluates the finite coefficient prefix for the requested degree. The family remains indexed by every natural degree even when the certificate uses only finitely many.

comparisons.note: The degree-d test is the sum of its coefficients through degree d. The family includes a test for every nonnegative integer d.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.FaceSegment.moment`. Selects a radial or height strip according to the segment direction. The weighted flag changes the radial measure only for height strips.

comparisons.note: The trace formula chooses the radial or height strip according to the face direction. The extra cylindrical weight r is inserted only in the height-strip case when requested.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsFaceSegment`. Requires a nonzero strip width, positive interval length and nonzero leading test coefficient at every degree. Finite polynomial tables need a continuation satisfying the last condition.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum`. The disjoint sum distinguishes gradient, velocity, side, pressure, corner, stream and extra-side data. The corner-stream block has no harmonic label, unlike the seven other blocks.

comparisons.note: The eight coordinate families distinguish volume gradients, volume velocities, side velocities, side gradients, pressure moments, corner velocities, corner stream values, and whole-side velocities. Only the stream-value family has no harmonic index.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.Datum`. Specialises the eight tagged blocks to the layout's harmonic set, degrees, segment counts and corners.

comparisons.note: The eight coordinate families use the harmonic set, polynomial degrees, segment counts, and corner count of the chosen cell layout.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.instDecEqDatum`. Provides classical equality for the finite tagged coordinate type. This instance is a logical convenience and is not a serialised comparison routine.

comparisons.note: Equality of two cell coordinates means equality of their family and all its indices. This logical identification supplies no prescribed comparison algorithm for a certificate file.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.instFintypeDatum`. Derives finiteness from the tagged product-and-sum construction. A decoder's packed ordering must agree with the chosen coordinate map.

comparisons.note: The cell coordinate set is finite because each of its eight families has finitely many indices. A file representation still needs an explicit correspondence with these coordinates.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.sideTest`. Radial faces use height polynomials; height faces use radial polynomials with an extra factor r on axis cells.

comparisons.note: A radial face uses a height basis polynomial. A height face uses a radial basis polynomial, multiplied by r when the cell touches the axis.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.RelIndex`. The tagged index separates derivative identities, divergence, axis conditions, stream identities and side-moment consistency. Different tags have different degree ranges.

comparisons.note: The ten relation families separate derivative identities, divergence, axis identities, stream identities, and compatibility of side moments. Each family retains its own degree ranges.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.segmentTestPair`. Integrates a supplied one-variable test against a segment polynomial over that segment's interval.

comparisons.note: The segment pairing integrates the supplied test times the segment polynomial over that segment's tangential interval.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.radialInt`. This helper uses ordinary one-dimensional measure; callers insert lineWeight explicitly when it is needed.

comparisons.note: The radial integral uses ordinary dr on [r₁,r₂]. Any cylindrical or polynomial weight appears in the integrand.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.heightInt`. Integrates over the closed height interval. Boundary endpoints have no extra mass in the integral.

comparisons.note: The height integral uses ordinary dz on [z₁,z₂]. Including the endpoints adds no mass.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.radialStiff`. Pairs a derivative of one radial basis polynomial with another, using lineWeight and the reference-interval vanishing factor.

comparisons.note: The radial derivative entry pairs a differentiated radial polynomial with another basis polynomial, using the radial measure and the factor 1−ξ² in the reference coordinate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.heightStiff`. Pairs a height derivative with a basis polynomial using the corresponding reference-interval factor.

comparisons.note: The height derivative entry pairs a differentiated height polynomial with another basis polynomial, multiplied by 1−η² in the height reference coordinate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.radialShift`. Represents multiplication by r in the weighted radial basis through an integral of two basis polynomials.

comparisons.note: Multiplication by r has matrix entries ∫w(r)r pᵢ(r)pⱼ(r)dr in the radial basis.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.unitAt`. Returns the row that reads one tagged datum. It is an exact algebraic coordinate selector.

comparisons.note: The coordinate row is 1 at the selected coordinate and 0 elsewhere, so pairing it with a data vector reads that entry.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.strainAt`. Returns the coordinate row when both degrees lie through Q, and the zero row otherwise. The fallback is intentional and must not mask a malformed stored index.

comparisons.note: The gradient row selects the specified coefficient when both degrees are at most Q and is zero outside that range.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.velocityAt`. Returns a velocity-coordinate row only for degrees below Q, with zero outside that range.

comparisons.note: The velocity row selects the specified coefficient when both degrees are below Q and is zero otherwise.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.turnRow`. Combines multiplication by the angular frequency with rotation of the cylindrical basis. The radial and angular components acquire opposite frame-coupling terms.

comparisons.note: For angular frequency k, the angular velocity derivatives are ikvᵣ−vφ, ikvφ+vᵣ, and ikv_z. The extra terms arise from rotation of the cylindrical frame.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.extraAt`. Returns an extra-side coordinate row through degree Q and zero beyond it.

comparisons.note: The auxiliary whole-side row selects the requested coefficient through degree Q and vanishes for larger degrees.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.streamAt`. A present corner selects its stream coordinate; an absent corner contributes zero. Layout validity restricts the absence to the permitted axis case.

comparisons.note: A represented corner contributes its stream-function coordinate. An omitted corner contributes zero; valid geometry limits this case to the permitted axis endpoint.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.zeroMode`. Looks up zero in the layout's finite mode set. The optional result controls axis and stream relations that exist only for that mode.

comparisons.note: The zero angular mode is available precisely when 0 belongs to the selected mode set. Axis and stream relations use this membership test.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.radialBeta`. Axis cells use powers r^(i+2), while off-axis cells use r^i. The shifted exponent supports the axis boundary identities.

comparisons.note: The radial integration test is r^(i+2) on an axis cell and rⁱ off the axis. The shifted powers enforce the axis-compatible boundary identities.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.relationRow`. Builds the ten families of exact linear relations from differentiation, divergence, axis behaviour and trace matching. Some index cases deliberately produce zero rows; independent selected rows are checked later.

comparisons.note: The ten linear relation families express derivative, divergence, axis, stream, and side-moment identities. Zero-degree and absent-mode cases can give zero rows, so the selected elimination block must be checked separately for invertibility.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.IsSkeletonDatum`. Marks side velocity, side gradient, pressure, corner velocity and corner stream blocks as skeleton data. Volume and extra-side coefficients are excluded.

comparisons.note: Boundary coordinates comprise side velocity, side gradient, pressure moments, corner velocity, and corner stream values. Volume coefficients and auxiliary whole-side moments lie outside this set.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsCellLayout`. Matches the abstract cell data, degrees and bases, then imposes exact side placement, coverage and orthonormal trace tests. Axis omissions and polynomial degree restrictions are explicit parts of the predicate.

comparisons.note: The layout must match the given cell, modes, degrees, and orthonormal bases, with correctly placed segments and corners. Its conditions also require side coverage, disjoint segment interiors, and the stated axis exceptions.

comparisons.note: Every selected elimination row must be one of the exact cell relations, and every retained boundary coordinate must belong to an allowed boundary family. The selected solved block must have nonzero determinant.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.cornerAt`. Reads a corner component when the cell-corner map is present and otherwise gives zero. The layout predicate controls which axis corners can be omitted.

comparisons.note: The corner row reads the selected velocity component when that corner is represented and gives zero for an omitted corner. The layout conditions control the axis omissions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.sideGradientRow`. Combines segmented gradient moments with the integrals of a whole-side test against each segment test polynomial.

comparisons.note: The whole-side gradient moment is the sum of the segment moments, weighted by the pairings of the whole-side test with each segment test.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.sideRadius`. Uses r₁ for side zero and r₂ otherwise. Its geometric interpretation requires the caller to be in a radial-side branch.

comparisons.note: The inner radial side has radius r₁ and the outer radial side has radius r₂. The formula is used in the radial-side cases.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.sideHeightIndex`. Maps whole-side number two to the lower height endpoint and the other branch to the upper one.

comparisons.note: For height sides, side 2 selects the lower endpoint and side 3 selects the upper endpoint.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.sideRadialIndex`. Maps side zero to the inner radial endpoint and the other branch to the outer endpoint.

comparisons.note: For radial sides, side 0 selects the inner endpoint and side 1 selects the outer endpoint.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.sideVelocityRow`. Combines velocity moments on the side's segments, retaining the q+2 test range.

comparisons.note: The whole-side velocity moment combines the moments on its segments using test degrees from 0 through q+1.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.turnSideRow`. Applies the angular-frequency and cylindrical-frame terms to the assembled side velocity row.

comparisons.note: The angular derivative of a side moment combines ik times that moment with the cylindrical-frame corrections −vφ and +vᵣ in the first two components.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.faceBaseRow`. Reconstructs a face gradient from tangential integration by parts, angular frame terms or stored normal derivative moments, according to the component and face.

comparisons.note: Gradient traces are recovered by tangential integration by parts, the angular frequency and frame terms, or the supplied normal-derivative moments. The chosen formula depends on the face and differentiation direction.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayout.strainFaceRow`. Replaces the normal diagonal entry by minus the other two diagonal entries. This implements the divergence-free trace constraint on either kind of face.

comparisons.note: On each face, the normal diagonal gradient entry is replaced by minus the other two diagonal entries. This enforces zero divergence in the reconstructed trace.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.radialWeightIntegral`. Integrates ρ times the supplied test function from zero to r. This is a helper for weighted trace identities, rather than a new certificate condition.

anchor.heading: Primitive of the radial test weight (L824)

comparisons.note: The primitive is ∫₀ʳρt(ρ)dρ, retaining the cylindrical factor ρ used in the trace identities.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.formOfRows`. The returned matrix is the conjugate-row pullback of the supplied form. Complex conjugation is on the first row factor.

anchor.heading: Pull a form back along rows (L854)

comparisons.note: If R is the matrix of rows, the form on the original coordinates is R*GR. Complex conjugation falls on the first row factor.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.testSupForm`. Pulls back the inverse test Gram matrix. The inverse is total in Lean; the analytical use needs the separate positive-definiteness hypotheses.

anchor.heading: Form from an inverse Gram matrix (L857)

comparisons.note: The test form is R*G⁻¹R for the matrix R of test rows. Positive definiteness of G is required when interpreting this expression as the optimal bound from those tests.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.LowIndex`. Abstracts the map from a cell's gradient and velocity coefficients and face rows to a larger coordinate set.

comparisons.note: The data locate gradient and velocity coefficients in a common coordinate vector and supply radial- and height-face moment rows. The gradient degrees run through Q, while the velocity degrees are below Q.

comparisons.note: The data specify the map from a harmonic, ordered gradient component and two degrees to its coordinate.
