passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.basisFn`. Multiplies one radial and one height basis polynomial, with normalisation supplied by the basis predicate.

comparisons.note: The two-variable basis function is the product pⱼ(r)qₗ(z). The separate basis conditions determine its normalization.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.monomial`. Uses ordinary r and z powers, unlike CellPoly.eval, which uses affine reference coordinates.

comparisons.note: The monomial is rʲzˡ in the physical meridian coordinates. Cell-model coefficients expressed in affine coordinates use a different evaluation formula.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialSlope`. Differentiates a real test function while fixing height; regularity is a separate mathematical input.

anchor.heading: Radial derivative of a real test (L872)

comparisons.note: This derivative is ∂ᵣf(r,z) for a real test f, with height fixed.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightSlope`. Differentiates a real test function while fixing radius.

anchor.heading: Height derivative of a real test (L874)

comparisons.note: This derivative is ∂zf(r,z) for a real test f, with radius fixed.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.rectIntegral`. Uses ordinary two-dimensional measure. Callers supply the cylindrical or polynomial-basis radial weight explicitly.

comparisons.note: The integral is over the meridian rectangle with measure dr dz. A radial weight must be included explicitly in the integrand.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.testInnerMatrix`. Forms a complex matrix from real weighted integrals of pairs of tests. It does not itself assert positivity of the weight or matrix.

comparisons.note: The test Gram matrix has entries ∫_Q mPᵢPⱼ dr dz. Its entries are real, even when the matrix is subsequently used on complex coordinates.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.frameTurn`. Records the two nonzero coefficients that couple radial and angular basis directions under rotation.

comparisons.note: The frame-rotation matrix has the two nonzero entries corresponding to ∂φeᵣ=eφ and ∂φeφ=−eᵣ.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularComb`. Combines the harmonic frequency with frame rotation in both indices of a gradient array.

comparisons.note: The angular derivative of a gradient component contains the frequency term ik and frame-rotation terms in both component indices.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularArray`. Applies angularComb to a linear combination of gradient components, retaining both frame corrections.

comparisons.note: For a chosen linear combination of gradient entries, the angular coefficient array is obtained by summing the frequency and two frame-rotation contributions for each entry.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.unitArray`. The coefficient array isolates a single ordered gradient entry, without imposing symmetry.

comparisons.note: The coefficient array equals 1 at the chosen ordered pair of gradient indices and 0 elsewhere.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.curlArray`. The alternating array extracts the appropriate difference of gradient entries with the same convention as curlComp.

comparisons.note: The coefficient array uses the alternating symbol to extract one curl component from the gradient, with the differentiation index in the second gradient position.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.lowRow`. Combines low-gradient coordinate selectors with the supplied component array at one harmonic and one polynomial index.

comparisons.note: At a fixed harmonic and polynomial index, the row is the chosen linear combination of gradient coordinates.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialFaceComp`. Combines stored radial-face rows with an array selecting gradient or curl components.

comparisons.note: The radial-face row combines the nine component trace rows with the supplied coefficient array, allowing either gradient or curl combinations.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightFaceComp`. The height-face version keeps the same component convention and its own polynomial-index direction.

comparisons.note: The height-face row combines the component traces with the same coefficient array and the height-face test index.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.lowPairRow`. Expands a test pairing through the known low-gradient coefficients, using integrals against tensor-product basis functions.

anchor.heading: Pair a polynomial test with data (L909)

comparisons.note: The test pairing sums the known gradient coefficients against the integrals of the test times the tensor-product basis functions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightMoment`. Integrates a power of z against a height basis polynomial over the cell interval.

comparisons.note: The height moment is ∫zˡqₗ′(z)dz over the height interval.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialMoment`. Integrates a power of r against a radial basis polynomial with the axis-dependent lineWeight.

comparisons.note: The radial moment is ∫w(r)rʲpⱼ′(r)dr, with w(r)=r on axis cells and w(r)=1 elsewhere.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialProjForm`. Forms the derivative contribution already determined by low coefficients, including innerRadius and the reference vanishing factor.

comparisons.note: The known radial derivative energy is a quadratic form in the low polynomial coefficients. Its integral contains the radial measure, the lower radial comparison factor, and 1−ξ² in the reference coordinate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightProjForm`. Forms the corresponding height derivative contribution using the height reference coordinate.

comparisons.note: The known height derivative energy uses the same low coefficients and radial comparison factor, with the height derivative and factor 1−η².

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialInnerWeight`. The weight combines r−r₁ with the radial reference vanishing factor and is used by the off-axis inner form.

comparisons.note: The interior radial weight is (r−r₁)(1−ξ²), where ξ is the radial reference coordinate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightInnerWeight`. Combines r−r₁ with the height reference vanishing factor for the off-axis inner form.

comparisons.note: The interior height weight is (r−r₁)(1−η²), where η is the height reference coordinate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialInnerForm`. Uses an inverse Gram matrix on degrees below Q−1 in radius and through Q in height. Natural subtraction makes the index empty for small Q.

comparisons.note: The radial interior form uses integration by parts and the inverse test Gram matrix, with radial degrees below Q−1 and height degrees through Q. This family is empty when Q≤1.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightInnerForm`. Uses the integration-by-parts test family with degrees below Q in both variables and the height inner weight.

comparisons.note: The height interior form uses the differentiated weighted tests and their Gram matrix, with both test degrees below Q.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialOuterTest`. Multiplies a meridian monomial by the basis lineWeight; this is a test function, not a coordinate value.

comparisons.note: The outer radial test is w(r)rʲzˡ, where w is the axis-dependent polynomial measure.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialOuterRow`. Combines moments on both radial faces with a differentiated interior test. The displayed plus signs follow the reference-coordinate factors already included in the formula.

comparisons.note: The outer radial row combines both face moments with the interior derivative of rξ times the weighted test. The endpoint values ξ=−1 and ξ=1 account for the two positive face terms.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialOuterForm`. Pairs the radial outer rows through the inverse Gram matrix with cylindrical weight r.

comparisons.note: The outer radial derivative form pairs these boundary rows through the inverse Gram matrix with cylindrical measure r dr dz.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightOuterRow`. Combines height-face moments and an interior derivative of r times the height reference coordinate and test monomial.

comparisons.note: The outer height row combines the two height-face moments with the negative height derivative of rηrʲzˡ in the interior.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightOuterForm`. Uses the inverse Gram matrix for height outer rows, with the radial and height degree ranges in their stated order.

comparisons.note: The outer height form uses the inverse Gram matrix with cylindrical weight r and test degrees through q radially and through Q vertically.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularTest`. Adds a factor r to the monomial so that the angular test family has the required axis behaviour.

comparisons.note: The axis-compatible angular test is r^(j+1)zˡ, obtained by multiplying the meridian monomial by r.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularAxisForm`. Uses the axis-compatible tests and a Gram matrix with radial weight r, avoiding a separate inverse-radius diagonal term.

anchor.heading: Angular energy on an axis cell (L965)

comparisons.note: The angular form on axis cells uses the r-weighted Gram matrix of axis-compatible tests. Its bounds come from their pairings with the known coefficients.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularOffWeight`. The weight is (r₂−r)/(r r₂); the off-axis branch and valid cell provide the positivity and denominator conditions.

comparisons.note: The off-axis angular weight is (r₂−r)/(rr₂). It is nonnegative on a valid off-axis interval and vanishes at r₂.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularOffForm`. Adds an inverse-r₂ diagonal form to a weighted test-supremum remainder. It is selected only in the off-axis component form.

comparisons.note: The off-axis angular form adds the diagonal contribution 1/r₂ to a remainder obtained from tests weighted by (r₂−r)/(rr₂).

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.componentForm`. Combines radial, height and angular contributions, choosing different constructions on and off the axis.

comparisons.note: The component energy adds radial, height, and angular contributions. Axis cells omit the off-axis interior terms and use the axis-compatible angular tests.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.topForm`. Selects the upper degree strips of two gradient-column blocks. Its use of Q−1 is natural-number subtraction.

comparisons.note: The penalty selects the upper polynomial-degree strips in the radial and height columns of the gradient. When Q=0, the lower threshold Q−1 is taken to be zero.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.energyForm`. Sums component derivative forms with mode weights and subtracts the prescribed highest-degree penalty.

comparisons.note: For each mode, the form adds weighted gradient and curl derivative energies and subtracts the designated highest-degree penalty. The result is then summed over the resolved modes.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.LowSlot`. The two constructors distinguish a nine-component gradient basis element from a three-component velocity element, with different degree cutoffs.

comparisons.note: A low polynomial coordinate belongs either to a gradient component with degrees through Q or to a velocity component with degrees below Q.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.slotValue`. A gradient slot has zero velocity and a velocity slot has zero gradient. Each nonzero component is one tensor-product basis function.

anchor.heading: Field represented by one low slot (L1005)

comparisons.note: A single low coordinate represents one tensor-product basis function in its chosen component. The other components and the other field, velocity or gradient, are zero.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.slotIndex`. Routes a gradient or velocity slot through the corresponding map in LowIndex.

anchor.heading: Embed a low slot in cell data (L1013)

comparisons.note: The selected gradient or velocity coefficient is placed in the common data vector using the appropriate coordinate map.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.slotRow`. The row is one at the embedded slot and zero elsewhere; it includes a harmonic label as well as the slot constructor.

comparisons.note: The row reads one low coefficient at its harmonic and component-degree position, taking value 1 there and 0 elsewhere.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.matrixSesq`. Evaluates the full complex sesquilinear expression on two packed 12-component vectors, before a real part is taken elsewhere.

comparisons.note: The paired local form is U*AU′ on two 12-component vectors. This expression remains complex-valued until a real part is explicitly taken.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.layoutIndex`. Connects abstract LowIndex to the tagged CellDatum slots and translates two radial plus two height faces into the four-side numbering.

anchor.heading: Low rows supplied by a layout (L1030)

comparisons.note: The chosen cell layout supplies the low-coefficient locations and the trace rows. Its four faces are ordered as two radial faces followed by two height faces.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.polyFn`. Describes functions representable by complex coefficients with separate radial and height degree cutoffs. It is a set of functions, not a stored coefficient array.

comparisons.note: The polynomial space consists of complex functions with degree at most d in r and at most d′ in z. Its description is by the existence of a finite coefficient expansion.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.pairOn`. Integrates F times the complex conjugate of the test polynomial with a supplied real weight.

comparisons.note: The weighted pairing is ∫_Q m F conjugate(P) dr dz, with conjugation on the test function.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.normSqOn`. Integrates the squared complex modulus against a supplied weight. Nonnegativity requires the weight assumptions used by the estimate.

comparisons.note: The weighted square is ∫_Q m|F|² dr dz. A nonnegative weight is needed for its interpretation as a squared seminorm.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.lineWeightFn`. Lifts the one-dimensional basis weight to the meridian rectangle without introducing a height dependence.

anchor.heading: Radial basis weight on the cell (L1542)

comparisons.note: The two-dimensional basis weight depends only on r: it is r for an axis cell and 1 for an off-axis cell.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.proj`. Chooses a polynomial orthogonal residual when such a polynomial exists, and returns zero otherwise. The analytic projection properties require the separate existence and uniqueness arguments.

comparisons.note: The selected polynomial has a residual orthogonal to every polynomial within the prescribed degree bounds. If no such polynomial exists, the formula gives zero; the analytic projection arguments establish the appropriate existence and uniqueness.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.tailNormSq`. Measures the residual after projection through degree Q in both variables, with the polynomial-basis radial weight.

comparisons.note: The tail square is the weighted integral of |F−Π_QF|², where the projection includes degree Q in both meridian variables.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.sesqValue`. Evaluates the real part of the complex form on the packed gradient-velocity vector, using conjugation on its first factor.

comparisons.note: The local value is Re(U*AU) on the 12 gradient-and-velocity coordinates, with conjugation on the first factor.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.supremumLoss`. Implements the three terms of L(G,v): curl, mixed gradient-velocity, and a Young-inequality split with length ℓ. Positivity of ℓ is a separate requirement.

comparisons.note: The stretching majorant is λ|curl G|²+√(7/2)g₀|G||v|+√(7/2)g′(ℓ|G|²+|v|²/ℓ)/2. The balancing length must be positive in the estimates that use it.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.quadForm`. Takes the real part of the conjugate matrix pairing. It uses the same convention as the local Hermitian forms.

comparisons.note: The complex matrix form is Re(x*Ax), using the standard conjugate pairing.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.inverseWeightedSq`. Evaluates the form of D inverse on a complex vector. Positive definiteness of D makes this a squared norm; the total matrix inverse alone supplies no positivity.

comparisons.note: The inverse-weighted value is Re(a*D⁻¹a). Positive definiteness of D makes this the squared norm associated with D⁻¹.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.realQuadForm`. Casts every real matrix entry to complex numbers before taking the real quadratic form. This is not an entrywise absolute-value bound.

comparisons.note: A real matrix acts on complex coordinates after its entries are regarded as complex numbers, and the real part of x*Ax is taken.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCoefficients.ofPieces`. Reads the class and harmonic-dependent weights into the five scalar coefficients. The subtraction of c in I₂ and the share term in I₂′ remain explicit.

comparisons.note: The Hessian coefficient is D−c and the curl-gradient coefficient is 1−share−D. The remaining entries are the curl coefficient after subtracting Z, the gradient coefficient, and the velocity coefficient of the chosen harmonic.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.tailGain`. The gain combines the first omitted radial/height eigenvalue with the positive-part angular gain. Axis cells use innerRadius=1 in the radial factor.

comparisons.note: The omitted-mode gain combines the smaller first omitted radial or height eigenvalue, multiplied by the lower radial factor, with (k−s)₊²/r₂. The angular shift s is chosen for the relevant field.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.hessTailGain`. The angular shift is 2 for a gradient tensor, giving the (|κι₁|−2)₊ term in (B.27).

comparisons.note: For a gradient tensor the shift is 2, giving (k−2)₊²/r₂ in the tail gain. In the application k is the magnitude of the angular frequency.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.curlTailGain`. The angular shift is 1 for a vector such as curl v, giving the corresponding omitted-mode gain.

comparisons.note: For a vector such as the curl, the shift is 1, giving (k−1)₊²/r₂ in the tail gain.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.velTailGain`. The velocity coefficients use degree Q−1, so the first omitted spectral level is Q instead of Q+1.

comparisons.note: Velocity coefficients have degrees below Q, so their first omitted spectral level is Q. The gain is min(Λʳ_Q,Λᶻ_Q).

comparisons.note: One exceptional set of meridian points is allowed for the residual estimate, and outside it the estimate holds for all times and angles. The high and long component bounds remain pointwise.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsMatOrthogonal`. Every label and matrix component has the corresponding zero polynomial moments, again with ordinary meridian-plane measure.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.turnVector`. The operator ikx plus the frame-rotation correction mixes the radial and angular components, while the vertical component has only ikx₃.

anchor.heading: Angular derivative in a moving frame (L4494)

comparisons.note: For angular wave number k the frame derivative sends (xᵣ,xφ,x_z) to (ikxᵣ−xφ,ikxφ+xᵣ,ikx_z).

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.testGrad`. Radial and vertical columns use spatial derivatives; the angular column is turnVector divided by r. Axis regularity is checked separately.

anchor.heading: Gradient of a harmonic test field (L4497)

comparisons.note: The gradient uses radial and vertical derivatives in those two columns; its angular column is the frame derivative divided by r. A separate condition controls this quotient at the axis.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsTestSolenoidal`. The cylindrical divergence equation is multiplied by r, giving ∂r(rϕr)+ikϕφ+r∂zϕz=0 throughout the cell rectangle.

comparisons.note: Divergence freedom is written as ∂ᵣ(rφᵣ)+ikφφ+r∂zφ_z=0 throughout the cell.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsAxisRegularTest`. The angular numerator is bounded by a constant times r on the entire cell, controlling the division by r in the angular derivative.

anchor.heading: Axis regularity of a test field (L4506)

comparisons.note: Each component of the angular derivative numerator is bounded by Cr on the whole cell, giving the required control near r=0.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sideTestMoment`. The face-moment routine receives the scalar test and both meridian derivatives, with its non-pressure convention selected explicitly.

anchor.heading: Test moment on one face segment (L4509)

comparisons.note: The face moment is formed from the test value and its two meridian derivatives, with the velocity-and-gradient trace convention.

passages.quote: A radial and a height polynomial are multiplied and their real product is regarded as a complex value for the row integrals. Orthonormality of these families is imposed separately.

comparisons.note: The formula multiplies the two real polynomial values and regards the result as complex. It makes no orthonormality assumption on the polynomial families.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.frameWeight`. The cylindrical components of y are r,0,z; this helper inserts the corresponding component in the similarity-drift row.

comparisons.note: The position vector has cylindrical components (r,0,z), which supply the coordinate factor in the similarity drift.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownStrainRow`. The integral includes radial measure r, the conjugated test gradient and half the coordinate times the conjugated test value.

comparisons.note: The gradient row integrates the tensor basis against r times the conjugated test gradient plus one half of the coordinate times the conjugated test value.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownVelocityRow`. The velocity pairing is multiplied by i times the supplied physical frequency plus 1/2, with radial integration weight and conjugated test value.

comparisons.note: The velocity row is (iω+1/2) times the radially weighted pairing of the basis function with the conjugated test component.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sideGradRow`. The boundary coefficient has a negative outward-orientation factor; a radial side also contributes its constant radial coordinate.

comparisons.note: The gradient boundary row has the negative outward-normal sign; a radial face also supplies its fixed radial coordinate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sidePresRow`. The pressure trace pairs with the normal test component and the positive outward-orientation factor, using component r or z according to the side.

comparisons.note: The pressure boundary row has the outward-normal sign and pairs with the radial or vertical test component according to the face orientation.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownRowVector`. Only the low-gradient, low-velocity, gradient-side and pressure-side blocks receive coefficients; every other tagged coordinate block is zero.

comparisons.note: The own-cell row has nonzero entries only for low gradient, low velocity, gradient trace and pressure trace coordinates.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsTestOfShape`. The degree limits are (q,q−1), (q,q) and (q−1,q) for the r,φ,z components, with Lean's natural-number subtraction at q=0.

comparisons.note: For q≥1 the radial, angular and vertical test components have degree bounds (q,q−1), (q,q) and (q−1,q). At q=0 every occurrence of q−1 is taken as zero.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.couplingStrainRow`. Two alternating-symbol contractions encode the cross-product coupling, integrated against the basis, radial weight and conjugated test field.

comparisons.note: The gradient coupling is the double alternating-symbol contraction with the velocity model, integrated against the tensor basis, radial weight and conjugated test field.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.couplingVelocityRow`. The vorticity model enters the alternating-symbol contraction paired with a low-velocity coefficient and a conjugated test component.

comparisons.note: The velocity coupling uses the vorticity model in the alternating-symbol contraction with the conjugated test field, integrated with the radial measure.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.couplingRowVector`. The coupling acts only on the low-gradient and low-velocity blocks, with all boundary and auxiliary blocks zero.

comparisons.note: The model-coupling row acts only on low gradient and low velocity coordinates; its trace and auxiliary coefficients vanish.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.opBound`. The squared bound holds for every complex three-vector. Since c appears squared, nonnegativity of c must come from the surrounding charge conditions when needed.

comparisons.note: The requirement is |Au|²≤c²|u|² for every complex three-vector u. It constrains |c|; a positive bound c needs the separate sign conditions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsChargeBound`. The strain form, mean vorticity-gradient operator and its oscillating remainder provide s₁,s₂,s₃ on every resolved label and point of the cell.

comparisons.note: The cell bounds control the strain quadratic form, the angular-time mean of the vorticity gradient and its oscillatory remainder at every resolved mode and cell point.

passages.quote: The strain quadratic form is bounded above by s₁\|u\|² at all times and angles.

comparisons.note: The strain quadratic form is bounded above by s₁|u|² at all times and angles.

passages.quote: The squared action of the zero-harmonic vorticity-gradient matrix is bounded by s₂² times the squared vector norm.

comparisons.note: This clause bounds the squared action by s₂²|u|² and therefore permits either sign of s₂. A nonnegative value is required by the surrounding charge conditions.

passages.quote: The difference from that mean mode has operator bound s₃ at every time and angle.

comparisons.note: The difference from that mean mode has operator bound s₃ at every time and angle.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.keySeg`. Builds the segment used to interpret a common boundary key. Its unused opposite level is chosen as lev+1, so this helper must not be confused with a cell’s physical width.

comparisons.note: The boundary segment retains its level, endpoints and test coefficients; its auxiliary opposite level is assigned one unit above the given level.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.Leaf`. Leaves distinguish A₀, ordered cell blocks, signed null-pair occurrences and rectangle credits. The nested sum preserves these cases even when some index sets are empty.

comparisons.note: The leaves comprise the global form, ordered cell blocks, positive and negative occurrences of null-pair forms, and rectangle credits.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.leafFintype`. Combines the recorded finite enumerations to enumerate all four leaf kinds. It adds no numerical positivity condition.

comparisons.note: Finiteness of the supplied cell partitions, null pairs and credits gives a finite list of leaves. This enumeration imposes no inequality on their matrices.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.pieceForm`. Masks the cell matrix to a chosen row-part and column-part. An off-diagonal block need not be Hermitian by itself; its transposed partner is placed at the same node.

comparisons.note: One ordered block is selected by retaining entries in the chosen row and column parts and setting the rest to zero. The transposed block is assigned to the same node by a separate condition.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.creditEmbed`. Selects from each owning cell’s embedding the coordinates used by a rectangle credit. Different entries may come from different cells.

comparisons.note: The credit embedding gathers each required trace coordinate from the embedding of the cell that owns it.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.leafForm`. Converts cell blocks to real global forms, inserts each null pair with both signs, and doubles the rectangle-credit form. These factors are the assembly identity in (B.38).

anchor.heading: Real form attached to a leaf (L5089)

comparisons.note: A leaf contributes the real pullback of a cell block, a signed null-pair form, the global form or twice a rectangle-credit form, as appropriate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.leafNode`. Uses the relevant node field for each leaf kind, including a separate node for each sign of a null pair.

comparisons.note: Each leaf is assigned to its designated node; the two signs of a null-pair form may have distinct node assignments.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.tree`. Combines the tree data with candidate front matrices Vξ. The front matrices are witnesses supplied to the node and pivot-count conditions.

comparisons.note: A proposed family of front matrices completes the supplied tree data. One such family must satisfy the node inequalities and the pivot-count condition together.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.gaugeDir`. Places pressure gauge moments in the cell’s skeleton coordinates and zero in ports and both multiplier blocks.

comparisons.note: A cell gauge direction inserts its pressure moments in the resolved cell coordinates and assigns zero to all ports, forcing coefficients and pin coefficients.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeConditionsGiven`. Requires a unique root and one common family of front matrices that passes every node enclosure and the global pivot count. The existential witness is shared across all nodes.

comparisons.note: The tree has a unique parentless root, opposite ordered cell blocks share a node, and one common family of front matrices satisfies every node enclosure and the pivot count.

passages.quote: The designated root has no parent.

comparisons.note: The designated root has no parent.

passages.quote: Any node with no parent is the designated root.

comparisons.note: Any node with no parent is the designated root.

passages.quote: Transposed blocks of a cell matrix are attached to the same node.

comparisons.note: Transposed blocks of a cell matrix are attached to the same node.

passages.quote: One family of front matrices satisfies every node enclosure and the pivot-count condition.

comparisons.note: One family of front matrices satisfies every node enclosure and the pivot-count condition.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.unitMoment`. Computes the full face moment of a unit pressure value. Horizontal faces use a difference of weighted primitives, distinguishing this from a deleted-key endpoint weight.

comparisons.note: The unit-pressure moment uses the full boundary interval; on a horizontal face it is the difference of the weighted primitives at both endpoints.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.KeyInHalfPlane`. Requires positive radius for radial faces and corners, allows zero radius for horizontal segments and stream values, and imposes no geometry on private coordinates.

comparisons.note: Radial faces and corners must have positive radius; horizontal intervals and stream points may reach radius zero. Private interior coordinates impose no boundary-location condition.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.KeyPartOmitted`. A real or imaginary component may be absent through reality, plane parity or an explicit gauge deletion. The plane cases additionally require the key to lie in the permitted half-plane.

anchor.heading: Reasons to omit a key component (L5253)

comparisons.note: A component may be omitted because of reality, reflection parity or a specified pressure-gauge deletion. Reflection-based omissions also require the prescribed half-plane geometry.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.varDir`. Uses a cell-coordinate gauge value first; multiplier unknowns contribute zero; otherwise a common skeleton key supplies the gauge value. Missing keys contribute zero.

anchor.heading: Gauge action on a global unknown (L5257)

comparisons.note: The global gauge coefficient is taken from an assigned cell coordinate when present, is zero for a forcing coefficient, and otherwise comes from the associated boundary pressure moment.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.varPartDir`. Combines a gauge class with its conjugate class to obtain the real or imaginary coordinate direction. This is a pair of class directions, not ordinary numeric extraction from one entry.

comparisons.note: A gauge class and its conjugate class are averaged or differenced to obtain the direction acting on the real or imaginary global coordinate.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.GaugeRowTransport`. For every non-deleted cell key, its direct gauge direction equals the row representation acting on global gauge directions.

comparisons.note: For every cell coordinate that has not been deleted, its direct gauge coefficient must equal the row representation applied to the global gauge directions.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.GaugeKeyConditions`. Requires pressure gauges to lie in both left and right kernels of cell forms, to vanish on credit coordinates, and to reconstruct unit pressure moments.

comparisons.note: Pressure gauge directions annihilate each cell matrix from both sides, vanish on credit coordinates and collectively recover the moments of unit pressure.

passages.quote: The stored gauge classes satisfy all algebraic incidence and conjugation conditions.

comparisons.note: The stored gauge classes satisfy all algebraic incidence and conjugation conditions.

passages.quote: Every cell form and its adjoint annihilate each gauge direction.

comparisons.note: Every cell form and its adjoint annihilate each gauge direction.

passages.quote: Every rectangle-credit coordinate has zero gauge value.

comparisons.note: Every rectangle-credit coordinate has zero gauge value.

passages.quote: The sum of gauge-class moments equals the unit-pressure moment on each zero-mode pressure key.

comparisons.note: The sum of gauge-class moments equals the unit-pressure moment on each zero-mode pressure key.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.RealKeyConditions`. Checks that standalone skeleton unknowns carry the mode recorded by their label, and that every cell key lies in the permitted half-plane.

comparisons.note: Standalone boundary coordinates must carry the angular mode of their harmonic label, and every cell boundary coordinate must satisfy the half-plane geometry.

passages.quote: A pure skeleton unknown has the azimuthal mode specified by its harmonic label.

comparisons.note: A pure skeleton unknown has the azimuthal mode specified by its harmonic label.

passages.quote: Every cell skeleton key satisfies the half-plane geometry predicate.

comparisons.note: Every cell boundary coordinate satisfies the prescribed half-plane geometry.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyWithMode`. Replaces the mode in velocity, gradient, pressure and corner keys while preserving geometry; stream and private keys remain unchanged.

comparisons.note: The angular mode is replaced in velocity, gradient, pressure and corner coordinates while their geometry is retained; stream and private coordinates are unchanged.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyOnPlane`. Recognizes horizontal face keys at z=0 and corner or stream points on that plane. A private coordinate is never classified as a plane key.

anchor.heading: Key lies on the reflection plane (L6180)

comparisons.note: A plane coordinate lies on a horizontal face at z=0 or at a corner or stream point of that plane. Private coordinates are excluded.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyFlipSign`. Returns the frame parity for velocity and corner data, the opposite parity for gradient data, one for pressure, and the axial parity for the stream value.

comparisons.note: Velocity and corner values use the frame reflection sign, normal-gradient values use its negative, pressure uses +1 and the stream value uses the vertical sign.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.sideKeyGeom`. Extracts side orientation, level, interval, polynomial tests and degree from velocity, gradient or pressure keys. Other key types return none.

comparisons.note: A face coordinate determines its orientation, level, interval, test coefficients and degree. Corner, stream and private coordinates have no such face description.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.retileKey`. Changes a face key’s interval, polynomial test family and degree while keeping its field type, mode and orientation. Non-face keys are left as they were.

comparisons.note: Retiling a face changes its interval, test polynomials and degree while retaining the physical quantity, angular mode and orientation.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.presUnitMoment`. Evaluates the face moment contributed by constant pressure, including the mode convention of the layout. Every non-pressure coordinate receives zero.

comparisons.note: The pressure-trace coordinate receives the face moment of constant pressure under the specified harmonic convention; every other coordinate receives zero.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.headUnit`. Extends the constant-pressure moment to a single resolved harmonic of the full cell-coordinate vector, with zeros in the other harmonics, ports and multiplier blocks.

comparisons.note: The constant-pressure direction is inserted in one harmonic's cell coordinates and is zero on all other harmonics, ports and coefficient groups.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyVelNormal`. Recognizes a mode-zero velocity moment in the component normal to its radial or horizontal face. These are the keys that can be reconstructed from stream endpoint values.

comparisons.note: The test selects the normal component of a zero-angular velocity trace, whose flux can be recovered from endpoint stream values.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ConjDatum`. Matches each of the eight datum kinds with the opposite azimuthal mode and the same relevant geometry. Matching indices alone is insufficient when two layouts differ.

comparisons.note: Conjugate coordinates have opposite angular modes and matching components, polynomial degrees and geometry. The relevant interval, corner or basis data must also agree.

passages.quote: `Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.streamEnds`. Returns the lower or upper geometric endpoint, with the variable coordinate chosen according to the face orientation.

comparisons.note: The lower or upper endpoint is chosen along the variable coordinate of the face, with its fixed radial or height coordinate retained.

passages.quote: **exact-pin-target**: Bind target to the actual decoded profile-gradient pin value, for every α and pin index. A separately rounded target vector breaks the exact target_eq identity; on this route it is the reason the target-gap quantity vanishes.
passages.title: Identify the profile and target

comparisons.note: Every target pin value is exactly the pairing with the represented profile gradient, for all parameters and pin indices; hence the target gap vanishes on this route.

passages.quote: In the weak sense, the supplied field is g=S⁻¹∂θv+v/2+(y·∇)v/2=T_Sv+∆v. The diffusion term enters separately in the weak right-hand-side equation.
passages.title: Perturbation with finite form energy

comparisons.note: In the weak transport identity, g represents S⁻¹∂θv+v/2+(y·∇)v/2, whereas the paper defines T_Sv=g−∆v in (7.1). Identifying g with T_Sv would add diffusion twice when the weak right-hand-side equation is formed.

passages.quote: Coordinate types, polynomial containers, linear maps and real or complex quadratic forms.

comparisons.note: This link gives a finite complex coefficient array for a polynomial in two cell coordinates. It supplies the polynomial part of the group described by the heading.
This link evaluates the coefficient array in the two affine cell coordinates. It supplies the polynomial evaluation mentioned in the surrounding representation guide.
This link collects multiplier weights, frame rates, transport functions, permutations, and forcing supports. These are representation choices within the broader group named by the heading.

passages.quote: **unlabelled-stream-block**: Corner-stream indices have no harmonic parameter. Multiplying this block by the number of modes silently changes every later packed coordinate position.
passages.title: Corner stream-function slot

comparisons.note: There is one stream-function coordinate per represented corner, independent of the number of harmonics.

passages.quote: Cell geometry, weights, mode sets, spatial support and the mesh complement.
