For this link, the finite mesh assigns each rectangle its resolved, tested, and eliminated modes and polynomial degrees.
For this link, the complement is the closed nonnegative meridian quadrant with the union of cell rectangles removed.

passages.section: Forcing support lies in the cells (L4832)
passages.quote: **support-radius-vacuity**: Do not infer a nonempty mesh from mesh_covers alone: H may be negative, and for k=0 the radius constraints are vacuous. Use the complete cell condition.

anchor.heading: Forcing support lies in the cells (L4832)

passages.title: Forcing support lies in the cells

comparisons.note: The mesh-cover condition alone can hold vacuously when H<0; if there are no forcing fields, the support-radius conditions do not rule this out. Nonemptiness must be inferred from the complete set of assumptions.

passages.section: Zero spline pieces after a cutoff (L1241)
passages.quote: **getd-support-default**: VanishesFrom quantifies over every natural i,j and reads a missing radial knot as 1. For a support cutoff below 1, all out-of-range radial pieces must also be zero; finite stored-piece checks need a matching continuation theorem.

anchor.heading: Zero spline pieces after a cutoff (L1241)

passages.title: Zero spline pieces after a cutoff

comparisons.note: Every polynomial whose radial left knot is at or beyond the cutoff must vanish, including all height indices. Missing radial knots are assigned value 1, so a cutoff below 1 also requires the corresponding out-of-range pieces to vanish.

passages.section: Polynomial joins of a chosen order (L2363)
passages.quote: **getd-join-default**: Knot reads in t_joins and x_joins default to zero, but their valid-mesh and interval-index guards keep these reads in range. Verify those guards exactly and use polynomial identities for every derivative through the required order.

anchor.heading: Polynomial joins of a chosen order (L2363)

passages.title: Polynomial joins of a chosen order

comparisons.note: Every joining identity is restricted to an active internal interface of a valid mesh, so the referenced knot is in range. The equality concerns every polynomial derivative through the required order.

passages.section: Joins across cells and the plane (L2372)
passages.quote: **reflected-derivative-sign**: At the symmetry plane, the o-th height derivative carries the factor (−1)^o. Equality of upper and lower coefficient arrays without that sign is not the required join.

anchor.heading: Joins across cells and the plane (L2372)

passages.title: Joins across cells and the plane

comparisons.note: Each half-chart has the required joins, both halves use the same radial knots, and their height derivatives at η=0 agree with the sign (−1)^o for order o.

passages.quote: **getd-core-and-outer-conjuncts**: The next-knot lookup defaults to one. Retain the valid index range and the independently required positive cutoff and knot membership; they are outside the universal implication and cannot become vacuous.
passages.title: Common constant near the origin

comparisons.note: The cutoff is a positive radial knot, and every active piece below it on either half has one common complex constant. The cutoff and knot-membership requirements hold independently of the universal conditions on pieces.

passages.quote: **nonnegativity-on-whole-chart**: The inequality covers every point of the unit square. A coefficient-based certificate can be sufficient only with the proved polynomial-to-value implication and the exact selected spline pieces.
passages.title: Nonnegative values on both charts

comparisons.note: The real part of each half-chart spline must be nonnegative at every point of [0,1]². A finite coefficient test needs a separate argument implying this value inequality.

passages.quote: **integer-decay-power**: Decode decay as an integer, not an unsigned count. Negative exponents are permitted by this data type and are controlled by the later shape and growth conditions.
passages.title: Piecewise constant auxiliary weight

comparisons.note: The auxiliary weight has upper and lower real step tables on a common mesh and an integer power of 1−σ. Negative powers allow growth towards infinity.

passages.quote: **active-piece-equality**: SplineAgrees compares active pieces only. Do not infer equality of the total piece functions outside their active ranges; separately check predicates such as VanishesFrom that quantify over all natural indices.
passages.title: Equality on active spline pieces

comparisons.note: Spline agreement means equal meshes and equal polynomials on all active rectangles. It places no requirement on unused interval indices.

passages.quote: **origin-profile-endpoint**: When the origin-profile edge equals 1, the tail-joining implication has a false guard. Preserve that allowed case; the physical chart of a valid L>0 field stays below 1.
passages.title: The joined origin correction

comparisons.note: The joining condition is required only when σ_g<1. At σ_g=1 it imposes no tail join within the chart, while physical points with L>0 have σ<1.

passages.quote: **shape-branch-and-axis-division**: Select the branch by exact ι₁=0. In the other branch division by κι₁ is legitimate only with positive κ and nonzero ι₁; keep the (1−η²)² and origin powers needed at the axis and origin.
passages.title: Divergence-free amplitudes

comparisons.note: The formula uses the stream-and-swirl construction (B.8) when ι₁=0 and construction (B.7) otherwise. The latter divides by κι₁, which is nonzero when κ>0 and ι₁≠0.

passages.quote: **compact-support-continuation**: VanishesFrom quantifies over all natural piece indices with a support-side default. A finite stored spline needs a continuation that vanishes outside the stored range, as well as the interior cutoff breakpoint and γ=0 clauses.
passages.title: Compact forcing-field shape

comparisons.note: Vanishing is imposed on all polynomial pieces whose radial left knot is beyond the cutoff, including missing indices whose assigned knot is 1. The separate breakpoint and γ=0 requirements must also hold.

passages.quote: **full-forcing-exclusion-rectangle**: The multiplier exclusion covers every lattice label in the j_* rectangle for every α∈K, not only the labels actually stored in a forcing field. Its two bounds are |ι₂|≤j_* and |ι₂−ι₁|≤j_*.
passages.title: Forcing modes avoid multiplier sets

comparisons.note: The forcing labels lie in |ι₂|≤j_* and |ι₂−ι₁|≤j_*. For every α∈K, every label in that entire rectangle avoids every signed λ- and μ-piece mode set.

passages.quote: **symmetry-normal-form**: A finite list of symmetry generators does not by itself prove that every element of the declared symmetry set has the required rotation/flip/integer-time form. Bind the set representation to this normal-form property.
passages.title: Allowed symmetry words

comparisons.note: Each declared symmetry has spatial action R_(aπ/κ)F^b and time shift a/2+j, with a a nonnegative integer, b either 0 or 1, and j an integer. Here F is the spatial flip.

passages.quote: The weight conditions prescribe joining orders, behavior at the origin, decay powers, and positive auxiliary steps, with 0<c,cμ<1. Nonnegativity is required for D, λ, and μ; no such condition on Z appears here.
passages.title: Admissible scalar weight shapes

comparisons.note: The displayed conditions do distinguish D, Z, λ, and μ by sign, joining order, and decay exponent. The added sentence about six auxiliary representation implications concerns a separate result and is not part of this condition.

passages.quote: **reciprocal-period-not-period**: Enclose 1/S(α) against periodInverse uniformly over K. An interval for S or a centre-point period error is not this bound unless it is converted with a proved positive-period enclosure.
passages.title: Uniform reciprocal-period enclosure

comparisons.note: The enclosure bounds |1/S(α)−s₀| uniformly on K. Converting a bound for S itself requires a positive lower bound for the period and the corresponding reciprocal estimate.

passages.section: Data fixed across the parameter set (L5011)
passages.quote: **uniform-parameter-equalities**: Check these equalities over the complete allowed parameter set; agreement at α=0 alone does not establish IsBoxUniform.

anchor.heading: Data fixed across the parameter set (L5011)

passages.title: Fixed data across the parameter set

comparisons.note: All equalities are required throughout K. Agreement only at the centre parameter does not establish parameter independence.

passages.quote: **weak-gradient-and-ae-symmetry**: Finite harmonic storage must establish the weak-gradient, period, integrability and almost-everywhere symmetry claims, not only a pointwise formula. The mode-support statement excludes the axis and uses physical modes derived from lattice labels.
passages.title: Regularity of each forcing field

comparisons.note: Each forcing field is measurable, period-one, uniformly bounded with bounded spatial support, and has finite L² norm and finite gradient norm. Its gradient is a weak gradient at each time; the discrete symmetries hold almost everywhere and the harmonic-support condition is imposed away from the axis.

passages.quote: **support-getd-default**: getD defaults to R, making the support guard true past the stored lists. All corresponding out-of-range coefficient continuations must be exactly zero.
passages.title: Jet coefficients beyond the support

comparisons.note: An absent breakpoint is assigned the support radius R, so the support condition forces the corresponding coefficient continuation to be zero.

passages.quote: **azimuthal-uniform-expansion**: The expansion holds for every time outside a spatial null set that may depend on that time, while amplitude rotation covariance is pointwise for every angle and point. Retain these distinct quantifier scopes and measurability obligations.
passages.title: Record the azimuthal dual bound

comparisons.note: For each time the harmonic expansion holds outside a spatial null set that may depend on that time. In contrast, the rotation law for each amplitude is pointwise in both angle and position.

passages.quote: **frame-column-in-offset-pairing**: The centre and linear frame pairings use frame l j, so j selects a column and l is summed against the forcing coefficients. Transposing this access changes the offset bounds.
passages.title: Require the offset enclosures

comparisons.note: The offset uses ΣₗVₗⱼβₗ, so j selects a column of V. Using Vⱼₗ would in general give a different offset.

passages.quote: **potential-phase-convention**: Preserve the integer time label, shifted azimuthal frequency and phaseIndex multiplier separately; they are different inputs to the complex exponential.
passages.title: Potential amplitude and phase

comparisons.note: The phase is the sum of the time-frequency term, the component-shifted azimuthal term and the radial-phase term, each with its own multiplier.

passages.quote: **complex-component-factors**: The half factors in the horizontal reconstruction are essential. Do not treat plus/minus amplitudes as independent Cartesian coordinates.
passages.title: Cartesian values from helical components

comparisons.note: The Cartesian reconstruction uses the factors 1/2 and 1/(2i): the circular components are x+iy and x−iy.

passages.section: Flux as a continuous linear map (L6783)
passages.quote: **flux-matrix-convention**: Keep the output-row/input-column convention when matching the paper’s div F_jᵀ. Frobenius norms survive transpose, but divergence orientation does not.

anchor.heading: Flux as a continuous linear map (L6783)

passages.title: Flux as a continuous linear map

comparisons.note: The flux matrix uses output components as rows and input directions as columns. Transposition preserves its Frobenius norm but changes the divergence contraction.

passages.quote: **jet-mesh-versus-jet-axis**: Do not replace IsJetMesh by IsJetAxis or assume it proves continuity. The flux conditions use the stronger predicate only in the direction needed for normal-flux continuity.
passages.title: Ordered jet breakpoints only

comparisons.note: Ordered breakpoints with fixed endpoints impose no continuity across intervals. The stronger matching conditions are required only in the normal direction of each flux component.

passages.section: Degree of freedom touches an end (L6803)
passages.quote: **end-cell-natural-subtraction**: Decode N−1 as truncated natural subtraction; for small N the endpoint conditions cover more degrees of freedom, rather than wrapping to a large unsigned index.

anchor.heading: Degree of freedom touches an end (L6803)

passages.title: Degree of freedom touches an end

comparisons.note: The threshold N−1 is zero when N=0. The endpoint conditions therefore include the indicated small-index cases without an unsigned wraparound.

passages.quote: **normal-flux-continuity**: Retain the asymmetric radialFlux_mesh and polarFlux_mesh requirements; they are what prevent surface-supported divergence terms at the respective partition seams.
passages.title: Potential joins and endpoint conditions

comparisons.note: Radial flux joins in the radial direction and polar flux in the polar direction. These are the matching conditions needed to avoid additional surface terms in the divergence.

passages.quote: **axis-ratio-default**: At r=0 on an axis cell, r/lineWeight(r) is 0/0 and hence zero in Lean. The simplification to one is valid only away from that endpoint; integral arguments must retain their domain conditions.
passages.title: Ratio of radial measures

comparisons.note: The measure ratio is r divided by the radial polynomial weight. It equals 1 for r>0 on an axis cell and takes the prescribed value 0 at r=0; the endpoint does not change integrals with respect to area measure.

passages.quote: **relation-guards-and-zero-rows**: Retain the ten tagged branches and their zero-degree, missing-mode and axis guards. The relation family contains intentional zero rows; selected rows must still satisfy the invertible solved-block condition.
passages.title: All cell relation rows

comparisons.note: The ten linear relation families express derivative, divergence, axis, stream, and side-moment identities. Zero-degree and absent-mode cases can give zero rows, so the selected elimination block must be checked separately for invertibility.

passages.quote: **credit-global-domains**: charge_between is global on ℝ², test_slope_bound is globally Lipschitz, and the side/top vanishing identities hold on entire lines. Restricting those checks to the closed patch changes the predicate.
passages.title: Credit rectangle conditions

comparisons.note: The charge bounds hold on all of ℝ², the Lipschitz bounds are global, and the boundary vanishing holds on the complete side and top lines. Restriction of all these conditions to the rectangle would be weaker.

passages.quote: **strict-and-nonstrict-floors**: Require hessFloor>0 on resolved modes but only curlHessFloor≥0. Do not silently turn non-strict admissible boundary cases into failed certificates or accept zero where the source requires a strict margin.
passages.title: The local analytic leaf inequalities

comparisons.note: The Hessian coefficient must be strictly positive on resolved modes, while the curl-Hessian coefficient is allowed to be zero.

passages.quote: **surrogate-slack-domain**: Prove exact forcing-gradient equality on every declared pairing label outside the slack set and exact pin equality on all labels. On slack labels use strictly positive weights and the full radial-weighted squared error sum; small pointwise samples do not imply that integral bound.
passages.title: Surrogate forcing-gradient pairings

comparisons.note: Forcing-gradient pairings are exact on declared pairing harmonics outside the error set, and pin pairings are exact on every harmonic. Inside the error set, positive weights and the full integrated squared-error sum are required.

passages.quote: **zero-complex-node-factor**: The factor is allowed to be zero. Together with positive pivot slack and slack_le this permits no real pivots at that node; it does not by itself invalidate a node with an empty pivot set. This is a source-level algebraic consequence, not a new Lean replay.
passages.title: Complex node enclosure conditions

comparisons.note: If the scale factor is zero, the upper bound for each real pivot slack is zero. Together with strictly positive pivot slack this forces the pivot set at that node to be empty.

passages.quote: **real-or-complex-witness**: Keep one chosen branch and all its shared existential data. Requiring both branches or allowing different matrices for separate fields misstates the proposition.
passages.title: Real or complex node certificate

comparisons.note: A node is accepted when either a real enclosure or a complex enclosure exists, together with the data and error matrices for that branch. Each branch uses one consistent choice of those data.

passages.quote: **missing-gauge-end**: Decode none as absence rather than a default class index; it changes the incidence direction.
passages.title: Gauge endpoint indicator

comparisons.note: An endpoint with no gauge-class assignment contributes zero to every class. It does not contribute to a default first class.

passages.section: Weight of a deleted pressure key (L4894)
passages.quote: **gauge-weight-nonzero**: A deleted key with zero weight cannot pass GaugeKeyValues.Conditions.weight_ne; preserve exact nonzero tests.

anchor.heading: Weight of a deleted pressure key (L4894)

passages.title: Weight of a deleted pressure key

comparisons.note: Every deleted pressure moment has a nonzero integration weight; a zero weight fails the stated gauge condition.

passages.quote: **exact-gauge-inverse**: Check the rational inverse and gauge-moment identities exactly or prove exact equality from their encoding; a residual near zero is insufficient.
passages.title: Valid pressure gauge data

comparisons.note: The rational incidence inverse and the gauge-moment factorization are exact identities. A small numerical residual alone does not satisfy them.

passages.section: Carry a complex form to real data (L5026)
passages.quote: **conjugate-pullback**: Use Re(P* Ψ P), with complex conjugation in the adjoint. A transpose-only or lower-triangle substitution changes the form.

anchor.heading: Carry a complex form to real data (L5026)

passages.title: Carry a complex form to real data

comparisons.note: The real pullback is Re(P*ΨP), with conjugation in P*. An ordinary transpose gives a different form for general complex P.

passages.section: Cell matrices on a rooted tree (L5030)
passages.quote: **abstract-types-need-decoders**: The finite types and function fields need explicit enumerations and interpretation from bytes. Tree.root already prevents an empty node type; no general positive-rank claim follows.

anchor.heading: Cell matrices on a rooted tree (L5030)

passages.title: The matrix tree data

comparisons.note: The finite coordinate and node sets need specified enumerations when interpreting numerical data. The chosen root makes the node set nonempty, without imposing a positive dimension on the other coordinate sets.

passages.section: Real form attached to a leaf (L5089)
passages.quote: **signed-leaf-factor**: Keep both signs of null pairs and the factor 2 for rectangle credits. Omitting an occurrence changes the assembled matrix.

anchor.heading: Real form attached to a leaf (L5089)

passages.title: Physical global and credit leaves

comparisons.note: Both signs of each null-pair form occur, and each rectangle-credit form is multiplied by 2. These coefficients are part of the assembly identity.

passages.quote: **shared-tree-fronts**: A separate successful choice of front matrix at each independently checked edge is insufficient: one consistent family must satisfy all node checks and the pivot count.
passages.title: Tree enclosure and pivot count

comparisons.note: One family of front matrices must satisfy all node enclosures and the pivot count simultaneously. Unrelated choices for separate checks do not supply this shared family.

passages.section: Gauge action on a global unknown (L5257)
passages.quote: **gauge-evaluation-priority**: Preserve the option-match order: a cell evaluation takes precedence over a multiplier evaluation; absent data contribute zero only in the stated branches.

anchor.heading: Gauge action on a global unknown (L5257)

passages.title: Gauge action on a global unknown

comparisons.note: An assigned cell coordinate takes precedence when a global unknown also has a forcing assignment. The other cases use the stated forcing or boundary-coordinate rules.

passages.quote: **two-sided-gauge-kernel**: Check both matrix and adjoint annihilation unless Hermitian symmetry has already been established for exactly this matrix.
passages.title: Gauge directions are invisible

comparisons.note: Each gauge direction is annihilated by both the cell matrix and its conjugate transpose. One condition suffices only after Hermitian symmetry of that matrix is established.

passages.quote: **conjugate-coordinate-geometry**: Validate the branch-specific equalities of boxes, bases, segments and corners; a negated mode label does not by itself identify a conjugate datum.
passages.title: Conjugate cell coordinates

comparisons.note: Opposite angular labels must also have matching components and the prescribed basis, segment and corner geometry. Label negation alone is insufficient.

passages.quote: **option-none-is-a-claim**: Do not treat none as a missing coefficient silently filled with zero. It must be justified by the specified symmetry, gauge or axis-stream condition.
passages.title: Valid stored or omitted component

comparisons.note: Omission of a real or imaginary component requires the specified reality, reflection, gauge or axis-stream condition. It is a mathematical condition on the absent coordinate.

passages.quote: **free-type-inhabited**: portRe : ℕ → Free supplies a free coordinate even when k=0 or no active ports are used. An empty Free type cannot decode this record.
passages.title: Sparse rows for global coordinates

comparisons.note: Assigning a free real coordinate to every natural port index forces the free coordinate set to be nonempty, even when no port is active and there are no forcing fields.

passages.quote: **sparse-row-support**: Treat rowVars as the declared finite support. A serializer with repeated indices must combine them consistently before it can represent this Finset-indexed row.
passages.title: Sparse complex row vector

comparisons.note: A row uses exactly its declared finite support, with one coefficient per global coordinate. Repeated numerical entries must first be combined into that coefficient.

passages.quote: **split-flux-denominators**: The raw formula permits zero denominators through Lean’s totalized division. SplitRow requires the appropriate denominator to be nonzero when that flux branch is used.
passages.title: Flux reconstruction on a subsegment

comparisons.note: The raw flux formula has assigned values even at zero denominators. Whenever the flux substitution is used, the subdivision conditions require its face radius or leading test coefficient to be nonzero.

passages.quote: **subdivision-cover-and-identities**: Check strict tile widths, adjacent endpoints, both outer endpoints and polynomial identities for every real argument. A pointwise quadrature check does not prove SplitRow.
passages.title: Check a subdivided moment row

comparisons.note: The subdivision has positive widths, matching adjacent endpoints and the exact outer endpoints. Each test-polynomial identity holds for every real argument.

passages.quote: **flux-rank-and-denominators**: Retain the radial positive-radius test, the horizontal nonzero leading coefficient and the smaller-rank dependency; the reconstruction formula alone is insufficient.
passages.title: Check a stream-flux row

comparisons.note: The radial flux case requires positive face radius; the horizontal case requires a nonzero leading test coefficient and an available linear moment of smaller rank.

passages.section: Solve a relation for one row (L6429)
passages.quote: **derived-row-acyclic**: Check the exact unit target coefficient, pressure cancellation and every strict rank decrease. Permitting a self-dependent cycle would change the justification.

anchor.heading: Solve a relation for one row (L6429)

passages.title: Solve a relation for one row

comparisons.note: The target coefficient is exactly 1, all pressure coefficients cancel, and each remaining dependency has strictly smaller rank. These requirements exclude cyclic reconstruction.

passages.quote: **unused-does-not-mean-zero**: Do not set an unused coordinate to zero when checking local inequalities. Its cell form and credit effects vanish, but InRowRange still permits an arbitrary complex value.
passages.title: Coordinate invisible to the forms

comparisons.note: An unused coordinate may take any complex value in the permitted row domain. Its reconstruction row, cell-matrix row and column, and credit contributions must all vanish.

passages.quote: **out-of-range-velocity-row**: Preserve the explicit zero fallback; use velReady when an actual lower-rank row is needed instead of assuming every natural index names a stored datum.
passages.title: Velocity-moment row with cutoff

comparisons.note: An out-of-range velocity moment returns zero. A row needed for reconstruction must separately have a valid degree, smaller rank and an active justification.

passages.quote: **normal-row-polynomial-identity**: The test derivative expansion must hold for every real argument, with radial factors and boundary signs preserved. Every velocity and corner row used must be ready.
passages.title: Reconstruct a normal derivative row

comparisons.note: The normal-derivative identity uses a polynomial equality for every real argument, with the stated radial factors and endpoint signs. Every velocity and corner row used is available at smaller rank.

passages.quote: **angular-inverse-domain**: Before using the inverse in turnedVec, check n≠0 and n²≠1 on eliminated modes; the raw matrix inverse is totalized outside that domain.
passages.title: Angular derivative matrix

comparisons.note: The angular inverse is used on eliminated modes only when n≠0 and n²≠1. These conditions exclude precisely the three singular integer frequencies.

passages.quote: **twelve-slot-order**: Keep gradient slots 0–8, velocity slots 9–11 and the condition j mod 3=1 exactly; changing the tensor order changes the eliminated form.
passages.title: Remove the angular velocity term

comparisons.note: The first nine entries are gradient components in order 3a+b, and the final three are velocities. The angular correction changes exactly the entries with b=1.

passages.quote: **zero-band-slack**: Do not divide numerically when bandSlack=0. Preserve Lean’s totalized value and check EliminationConditions.slack_zero, or impose and prove a strictly positive slack.
passages.title: Eliminated-harmonic form

comparisons.note: Zero slack is permitted only with exact equality between the source and its weighted approximation, making the divided remainder vanish. Positive slack uses the displayed quotient.

passages.quote: **row-full-inverse**: Use the full row matrix including the band correction; the positive-definite row weight and domination condition justify the inverse on the accepted path.
passages.title: Eliminated tested-row form

comparisons.note: The inverse uses the enlarged row matrix containing the eliminated-mode Gram correction. The positive base matrix and the domination inequality provide its positive lower bound.

passages.quote: **full-row-domain**: Check residual_value_le on every InRowRange vector, including its free unused, port, gauge and pressure-head directions; checking only the image of X_Q is insufficient.
passages.title: Local elimination comparison

comparisons.note: The residual form inequality holds on the full permitted row domain, including arbitrary unused coordinates, ports and complex gauge and constant-pressure directions.

passages.quote: **top-degree-boundaries**: Preserve the ≤ degree tests and the radial/vertical split; an off-by-one change loses highest-degree coefficients.
passages.title: Highest-degree coefficient charge

comparisons.note: The top-degree correction retains the stated non-strict degree inequalities and separates the radial and vertical derivative contributions.

passages.section: Gram matrix of tested row fields (L5540)
passages.quote: **row-gram-conjugation**: Use the declared i,i′ ordering and complex conjugation, together with the radial measure; a Euclidean coefficient dot product is a different Gram matrix.

anchor.heading: Gram matrix of tested row fields (L5540)

passages.title: Gram matrix of tested row fields

comparisons.note: The row Gram entry integrates the test indexed by i′ against the conjugate of the test indexed by i with radial weight r. It is an integral pairing of functions.

passages.quote: **row-bijection**: Validate both injectivity and surjectivity against the declared tested pairs. A missing or duplicate row cannot be repaired by a Gram check alone.
passages.title: Row enumeration and matrix bounds

comparisons.note: The row list is both injective and onto the declared harmonic-test pairs. Positivity of a Gram matrix alone does not check that enumeration.

passages.quote: **gradient-slot-order**: Keep slot 3a+b throughout matrix assembly, curl extraction and row tests; a transpose is not an innocuous storage change.
passages.title: Read the gradient slots

comparisons.note: Gradient component (a,b) is always placed at position 3a+b. Transposing these positions changes the curl, row tests and assembled matrices unless all formulas are changed consistently.

passages.quote: **split-matrix-not-projector**: bandProjection is stored as a matrix; the final PotentialConditions do not require idempotence or orthogonality. Use the supplied map in x−Px and Px instead of silently reconstructing a projector.
passages.title: Potential coupling data

comparisons.note: The splitting data supply a matrix P, with selected part Px and complementary part x−Px. Neither idempotence nor orthogonality is required by these conditions.

passages.quote: **strain-name-does-not-symmetrise**: Do not symmetrise this array in a decoder: strainOfVec is exactly gradOf with curried indices.
passages.title: Reshape the gradient entries

comparisons.note: The operation simply reshapes the full gradient entries; it leaves the antisymmetric part present.

passages.quote: **tail-degree-truncation**: The velocity degree uses natural subtraction d−1. Active layout conditions supply the relevant lower degree; do not reinterpret the subtraction as an unbounded integer operation.
passages.title: Tail of a coupling field

comparisons.note: The velocity projection degree is max(Q−1,0). The layout conditions supply the relevant degree bounds on the active route.

passages.section: Model harmonics active on this cell (L5753)
passages.quote: **active-model-labels**: A safe finite check may cover the union of all four support sets. Dropping a label requires exact vanishing throughout the cell of all 24 scalar coefficients, not an interval that merely contains zero.

anchor.heading: Model harmonics active on this cell (L5753)

passages.title: Model harmonics active in a cell

comparisons.note: A model harmonic is active if one of its 24 scalar components is nonzero somewhere on the cell. Omitting it requires exact vanishing of all components throughout the cell.

passages.quote: **potential-domain**: Prove the kept and port inequalities for all InRowRange vectors; retain its independent complex gauge, head, unused and port directions.
passages.title: Potential coupling conditions

comparisons.note: Both the retained potential comparison and the port estimate quantify the whole permitted row domain, including its free complex coordinate and pressure directions.

passages.quote: **pairing-zero-test**: gamma_resolved and gamma_other branch on nonzero almost-everywhere profiles. Omitting a profile requires exact a.e. vanishing, not small sampled values.
passages.title: Conditions for the pairing form

comparisons.note: The conditions are triggered by a pairing profile that is nonzero as an almost-everywhere function. Omitting that profile requires equality to zero almost everywhere.

passages.quote: **long-error-exact-zero**: The zero branch requires equality of both error bounds to zero. An interval containing zero or a numerical tolerance does not justify it.
passages.title: Reciprocal long-range row charge

comparisons.note: The zero long-error contribution requires both error bounds to equal zero exactly. Otherwise the reciprocal-cost term remains.

passages.quote: **natural-index-extension**: actuatorModel is indexed by ℕ and actuator_model_regular checks every natural index. A decoder that stores only k models must specify and validate a continuation, such as a justified zero extension.
passages.title: Conditions for tested row formulas

comparisons.note: Forcing approximations are supplied for every natural index, and the regularity condition applies to each one. A finite representation therefore also needs a specified valid continuation.

passages.quote: **row-range-free-directions**: Form the full real generator space, including unused and port real/imaginary unit vectors, complex gauge and head directions, and real β,ζ directions. Checking only rowEmbed’s image does not imply the three required local inequalities.
passages.title: All compatible local row vectors

comparisons.note: The admissible cell vectors include all real global row combinations together with complex gauge and constant-pressure directions, arbitrary complex unused coordinates and ports, and real forcing and pin coefficients.

passages.quote: **implication-scope**: Preserve antecedents and their polarity when expanding obligations; this declaration is not an unconditional copy of PotentialConditions or an independent list of eight new numerical checks.
passages.title: Potential checks after regularity

comparisons.note: The eight prerequisites are assumptions of an implication whose conclusion is the potential estimate. They are supplied by other parts of the final certificate argument.

passages.quote: **pressure-blind-two-sided**: pressure_blind requires zero rows and columns for several matrices plus zero source coefficients. Merely deleting pressure coordinates from one matrix check is insufficient.
passages.title: Assembly entries and exterior bounds

comparisons.note: Pressure coordinates have zero rows and columns in all the specified matrices and zero coefficients in the associated sources. Deleting them from one matrix alone does not establish these conditions.

passages.section: Validity on a full mode region (L3414)
passages.quote: **infinite-mode-set-coverage**: Class, membership and frequency bounds are required for every mode in the supplied set, which may be infinite. Give a finite case decomposition or exact lower-bound argument for the set; do not reduce it to the resolved modes.

anchor.heading: Validity on a full mode region (L3414)

passages.title: Validity on a full mode region

comparisons.note: Every label in the given mode set must have the common class, exact signed memberships, and stated frequency lower bounds. Every inward and outward coupling inequality must hold at every point of the region.

passages.quote: **all-labels-and-exterior**: The cover is over all integer labels and every half-plane point; enumerating only stored modes or sampled cells cannot establish it.
passages.title: Uniform coefficient lower bounds

comparisons.note: Coverage quantifies every integer harmonic and every quarter-plane point, including points outside all cells. It is not limited to stored or sampled modes.

passages.quote: **unresolved-is-infinite**: The quantifier is every harmonic not resolved, not merely every label in a stored finite list; include eliminated modes and the infinite remainder.
passages.title: Every unresolved mode is covered

comparisons.note: Every harmonic outside a cell’s resolved set is covered, including the eliminated modes and the infinite remainder of the lattice.

passages.quote: **exterior-no-cutoff**: Cover the actual unbounded exterior for every integer harmonic, with null overlaps and common charge identities. A large finite box cannot replace this predicate.
passages.title: Coverage of the unbounded exterior

comparisons.note: Every harmonic has a measurable cover of the unbounded exterior with null overlaps and common charges. A cover of a finite box is insufficient.

passages.quote: **nested-not-flat**: Retain shared existential witnesses in pair_surrogate, bound_valueSets and given_shape; the seventeen fields cannot be flattened into independent numerical assertions.
passages.title: The cell structure and constants

comparisons.note: The approximate-pairing budgets, field enclosures and shape data are shared choices within their respective conditions. They cannot be chosen independently for each scalar consequence.

passages.quote: **strictness-and-finiteness**: Preserve strict transfer, contraction and nontriviality inequalities. The .toReal gradient integral must be read with the full positive-weight hypotheses; an infinite integral is not a large finite number.
passages.title: Remaining certificate inequalities

comparisons.note: The transfer, contraction and nontriviality margins are strict where stated. The real-valued squared-gradient expression assigns zero to an infinite integral, so its use needs the complete admissibility conditions.

passages.quote: **different-gradient-exponents**: Use L² for centre_grad and L³ for box_grad, with the correct powers of their bounds. A single uniform L² error estimate cannot replace both.
passages.title: Reference and parameter shift bounds

comparisons.note: The centre gradient error is estimated in L², while the additional parameter change is estimated in L³, with squared and cubed bounds respectively.

passages.quote: **pin-equality-scope**: pinField_eq is an equality of full families over Fin k; do not restrict it to the selected adjointSet as with the preceding two equalities.
passages.title: Admissible potential and pin data

comparisons.note: The pin-matrix equality holds for the entire family of indices. The preceding potential and pin-generator equalities are restricted to active adjoints.

passages.quote: **conditional-certificate-boundary**: This is a premise about specific decoded data, not evidence that such data have been supplied. A checker acceptance must imply all fifteen fields for the same seven arguments.
passages.title: The fifteen cell conditions

comparisons.note: One shared choice of all seven data collections must satisfy all fifteen conditions. The implication supplies no particular numerical certificate.

Breakdown.SteadyCert.FracCertData.text: The data consist of steady spatial profiles, a parameter-dependent rotation rate, finite forcing and pinning families, and the constants used to bound their errors. The later time-periodic certificate supplies a separate family with a time variable.

Breakdown.CellCert.permSign.text: The alternating symbol is +1 on cyclic permutations, −1 on anticyclic permutations, and zero when an index repeats. These signs fix the orientation of the curl.

Breakdown.CellCert.FracCellData.text: The steady data are supplemented by a cell region, reference and polynomial model fields, approximation budgets, and spectral cutoffs. The associated conditions must establish the claimed bounds on these inputs.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.pinFiel.text: The pinning tensor Ξᵢ is obtained by evaluating its cell-polynomial matrix coefficients with the chosen symmetry order. Its pairing with a perturbation is defined separately.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.labelDe.text: The reduced mode density uses the parameter's period, weights, and harmonic bounds at normalized time zero and angle zero. The cylindrical factor r is inserted when integrating it.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.stretch.text: The expression first takes the positive part of the stretching density and then averages over one time period and all azimuthal angles. The order of these operations is retained.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.formPos.text: The positive reduced integral sums the nonnegative mode contributions and the averaged positive stretching contribution over the quarter-plane with weight r. Finiteness requires a separate estimate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsModeClass.text: The symmetry set contains the rotation by π/κ with a half-period time shift and the spatial flip with no time shift. These requirements give κ≥1 and do not require the whole symmetry set to be generated by these elements.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.HasMeasurableB.text: The transport majorants, four harmonic amplitude bounds, and the global vorticity and vorticity-gradient bounds must be measurable. This supplies the measurability needed in their integral estimates.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsHarmonicExpa.text: A finite set closed under negation reconstructs the field, its spatial gradient, and the supplied Hessian exactly at every time and point. The asserted identities concern the full functions.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.azimuthPhase.text: The angular phase is exp(iκnφ), containing only the spatial frequency and angle.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.patch.text: The trace patch is the closed rectangle [ρ₁,ρ₂]×[0,h]. Positive radius, width, and height are imposed when the patch is used analytically.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.patchGradSq.text: The modal Dirichlet density is |∂ᵣφ|²+|∂zφ|²+k²|φ|²/r². A patch separated from the axis avoids the radial denominator singularity.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.PlaneSegment.text: A trace segment provides its radial endpoints, a patch height, and finitely many real test functions of radius.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsPlaneSegment.text: The trace patch requires 0<ρ₁<ρ₂, h>0, and continuous test functions. These conditions keep its angular energy denominator away from zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.CrossWaveEntry.text: The wave data give finitely many angular modes of the gradient and second derivative, a meridian region, proposed operator bounds, and balancing parameters. Uniform inequalities must establish the bounds separately.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsCrossWaveEnt.text: For every point in the region, every angle, and every complex vector, the reconstructed symmetric strain and vorticity-gradient operators obey their squared norm bounds. The balancing parameters must also be positive.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsInstanceEn.text: The row, weight, forcing, pinning, and symmetry requirements all refer to the same cell data and their chosen representations.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyHess.text: The harmonic Hessian is its second spatial derivative as a complex vector field. The reference-profile construction later chooses representatives appropriate to its spline interfaces.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.realPartVe.text: The operation takes the real part of each of the three complex components. It is linear over the real numbers and is continuous.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeHess.text: The Hessian field sums the real parts of the second spatial derivatives of the individual complex harmonics.

Breakdown.CertReduction.gapGradCoeff.text: The gradient contribution to the profile gap uses either $2/(\sqrt{3}\sqrt{w_*})$ with an $L^3$ bound or the weighted supremum constant $c_w$ with an $L^2$ bound.

Breakdown.CertReduction.shiftGradCoeff.text: The $L^3$ contribution to the quadratic-form shift is $1/(\sqrt{3}\sqrt{w_*})$, half its contribution to the profile gap; the alternative $L^2$ coefficient is $c_w$.

Breakdown.CertReduction.ModelFormNumbers.text: The two proposed numbers are the lower strain bound s₋ and an L³ bound for the reference gradient, used to control the frozen quadratic form.

Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounde.text: Uniformly in α and time, the symmetric gradient is bounded below as a quadratic form and the cube of its operator norm is integrable. Their stated combination must fit within the frozen-form bound.

Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointQuadNumbe.text: For each adjoint, the data choose an L³ or L² estimate and provide a proposed norm bound; the associated validity condition supplies nonnegativity and the actual bound.

Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadCoeff.text: The quadratic adjoint coefficient is $2/(\sqrt{3}\,w_*)$ in the $L^3$ case and $c_w/\sqrt{w_*}$ in the $L^2$ case, before multiplication by the adjoint norm bound.

Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointSizeBound.text: The chosen inequality bounds either ∫|ψ|³ by n³ or ∫|ψ|² by n². Nonnegativity of n is imposed separately when these inequalities are used.

Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointQuadratic.text: For each j∈J, a nonnegative bound controls the selected adjoint norm at every time and every α∈K, and its weighted coefficient is at most ãⱼ.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.af.text: The supplied Hessian is combined with the same centre and tangent coefficients as the velocity field; any moving phase enters before this combination.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr.text: The Hessian expression uses the same moved phase and the same centre and tangent amplitudes as the approximate velocity.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is.text: The approximate velocity and its supplied Hessian equal the represented fields for every α, including values outside K. The target pin values are exactly the pairings with the profile gradient.
For every α, time and point, the prescribed pressure gradient equals ∇(qα−|Wα|²/2).
Every active adjoint equals its represented field for all α, hence is parameter independent. Each of its active harmonics has decay exponent at least 3.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.In.text: The profile, pressure and adjoint representation conditions must hold together, tying the analytic fields to the supplied harmonic data.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.withFor.text: Only the form coefficient c in the multiplier pieces is replaced; the other cell data, including the separately specified coercivity value, are retained.

Breakdown.CertCell.AdmissibleTuple.text: An admissible collection contains v, its weak derivatives, the time-and-dilation derivative, forcing coefficients and an L² right-hand side. The positive density must be finite for the explicitly chosen form coefficient.

Breakdown.CertCell.ContinuumConditionsGi.text: Three common enclosure constants work uniformly on K, reflection identities hold, and one coefficient-enclosure family covers the required modes and regions.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum.text: A gradient coordinate is specified by a harmonic, two component indices, and two polynomial degrees from 0 through Q.
A velocity coordinate is specified by a harmonic, one component, and two polynomial degrees strictly below Q.
A side-velocity coordinate contains a harmonic, segment, component, and test degree from 0 through q+1.
A side-gradient coordinate uses test degrees from 0 through q, one degree fewer than the side-velocity family.
A corner-velocity coordinate identifies one component of one harmonic at a represented corner. The geometry determines which corners require such coordinates.
There is one stream-function coordinate per represented corner, independent of the number of harmonics.
An auxiliary side-velocity coordinate identifies one of the four cell sides, a harmonic, a component, and a test degree from 0 through Q.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.Skele.text: A shared boundary coordinate is identified by its harmonic, geometric segment or corner, component, and complete polynomial test data. Coordinates internal to a cell carry a separate designation.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.keyOf.text: The boundary identifier retains the full test family and geometric location of each side or corner quantity. Volume and auxiliary whole-side coefficients remain internal.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.MeshS.text: The reconstructed segment preserves its face coordinate, interval, and test family, while choosing an auxiliary opposite coordinate one unit away. This auxiliary choice need not equal a physical cell width.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.text: The polynomial data give a degree bound d in each affine cell coordinate and a square (d+1)×(d+1) complex coefficient array. Leading coefficients may vanish.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.eval.text: The cell polynomial is evaluated in the affine coordinates ξ and η of the meridian rectangle. Coefficients given instead in powers of r and z require a change of basis.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.zero.text: The chosen zero polynomial has degree bound zero and its single coefficient is zero. Other all-zero coefficient arrays evaluate to the same function.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.text: For each cell, the vector data specify a finite set of active harmonics and three component polynomials. Only the active harmonic set contributes to the evaluated field.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.text: For each cell, the matrix data specify active harmonics and a polynomial for each ordered pair of cylindrical components. Coefficients outside the active set do not enter the field sum.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModelPolys.text: The model contains separate polynomial approximations for velocity, vorticity, strain, and the gradient of vorticity, together with an approximate reciprocal period. Error conditions link these approximations to the actual fields.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModelErrors.text: The error data distinguish the remainder left after polynomial, high, and long components from the separately bounded high components. They also include the error in the reciprocal period.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCharges.text: The three stretching coefficients s₁,s₂,s₃ and balancing length h depend on the harmonic and meridian point, as in (B.25).

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.text: Each real test row is assigned a cell, harmonic, polynomial test number, and real or imaginary part. The remaining data give the tests and weights for each cell-harmonic block.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.text: The cell data join the extended certificate, multiplier pieces, harmonic bounds, reference field, mesh, rows, models, pins, and coercivity constants. Their compatibility is established by the fifteen certificate conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCoefficients.text: The five coefficients multiply, in order, |∇²v|², |∇curl v|², |curl v|², |∇v|², and |v|². Their signs are constrained by the subsequent inequalities.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.scale.text: Scaling a polynomial multiplies all its coefficients by one complex scalar while retaining its degree bound.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.InstanceData.text: The interpretation data contain scalar weights, parameter-dependent frame rates, transport bounds, reflection permutations, and forcing harmonic sets. They also specify the common row-weight and forcing-frequency bounds.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.KeyAmp.text: For nonzero azimuthal index, the amplitudes use radial and polar splines A and B. The axisymmetric case uses stream and swirl splines S and T, a coefficient γ, and the origin and decay powers.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ShapeParam.text: All harmonic terms share the compactification length L, symmetry order κ, radial phase f, and origin function g.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.TimeFieldD.text: A finite set of pairs (ι,l) selects the active harmonics, while the amplitude data are specified for every possible pair.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.GivenShape.text: The reference profile has its own shared chart and phase parameters. Each forcing field may have separate parameters and a separate compactified support cutoff.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.bit.text: The scalar indicator equals 1 when the condition holds and 0 otherwise.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr.text: The profile data supply a common chart and phase, a radial cutoff and its parameter rates, together with separate centre and tangent harmonics and origin profiles.
A finite harmonic set and scalar spline amplitudes specify the pressure correction with the same time, angular and radial phase conventions as the velocity.
The centre and tangent pressure amplitudes are supplied separately; their shared radial phase can depend on α.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Ad.text: All adjoint harmonics share one chart and phase, with a separate finite harmonic field for each adjoint index.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellVar.text: A resolved cell coordinate identifies both its harmonic label and the corresponding coefficient or trace within that harmonic's cell coordinates.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellInde.text: The complete cell vector contains resolved-mode coordinates, complex auxiliary ports, forcing coefficients and pin coefficients in four separate groups.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellCalc.text: The cell calculus data combine harmonic coordinates, leaf bounds, model decompositions, local matrices, auxiliary ports, approximate pairings and ownership of the rectangle credits.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylRadiu.text: The cylindrical radius is $r=\sqrt{y_1^2+y_2^2}$, using the two horizontal Cartesian components.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylHeigh.text: The height is the signed third Cartesian coordinate z. Reflection to nonnegative height is a separate operation.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylPoint.text: The coordinate map sends (r,φ,z) to (r cosφ,r sinφ,z). Here φ denotes the spatial angle, as in the paper.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.radialUn.text: The radial unit vector is eᵣ=(cosφ,sinφ,0) in Cartesian coordinates.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.angularU.text: The azimuthal unit vector is eφ=(−sinφ,cosφ,0), the angular derivative of eᵣ.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.axialUni.text: The axial unit vector is $e_z=(0,0,1)$, independent of the spatial angle.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.azimuth.text: The angular frequency is κn for an integer n and symmetry order κ. This preliminary construction has one frequency index; the time-periodic construction uses a pair.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.text: The four numbers are the radial and height endpoints of a meridian rectangle. Its geometric validity is imposed separately by 0≤r₁<r₂ and 0≤z₁<z₂.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox..text: A rectangle meets the axis precisely when its inner radial endpoint satisfies r₁=0.
The meridian set is the closed rectangle [r₁,r₂]×[z₁,z₂]. Shared sides therefore remain in both adjoining rectangles.
The associated solid consists of points with r₁≤r≤r₂ and z₁≤|z|≤z₂. It includes all azimuthal angles and both reflected halves.
The radial polynomial measure has weight r on axis cells and weight 1 on cells separated from the axis. This is the Jacobi and Legendre distinction used in (B.27).
The radial reference coordinate is (2r−r₁−r₂)/(r₂−r₁). Positive cell width makes it the affine map from [r₁,r₂] onto [−1,1].
The height reference coordinate is (2z−z₁−z₂)/(z₂−z₁). The ordered height endpoints give the usual orientation from −1 to 1.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBo.text: The geometric requirements are 0≤r₁<r₂ and 0≤z₁<z₂. They exclude zero-width cells and justify the reference-coordinate denominators.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox..text: The lower radial comparison factor is 1 on an axis cell and r₁ on an off-axis cell, following the convention of (B.27).
The derivative is ∂ᵣP(r,z), with z held fixed. Its use as a classical derivative requires the appropriate differentiability of P.
The derivative is ∂P(r,z)/∂z, with r held fixed. The function may be complex-valued.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.text: The mesh data specify rectangles, resolved and tested harmonics, eliminated harmonics, and polynomial degrees for each cell and label. The geometry and compatibility of these choices are imposed by later conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.closedHalfPl.text: The closed meridian quadrant is {(r,z):r≥0,z≥0}, including both coordinate boundaries.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.region.text: The cell region is the union of all stored closed rectangles. It is empty when there are no cells.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.exterior.text: The exterior consists of the closed meridian quadrant with the cell region removed. The mode integrals are subsequently taken over the open quarter-plane.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.maxVolumeDeg.text: The maximum volume degree is taken over the resolved labels of the cell. It is assigned value zero when that set is empty.

Breakdown.CertCell.IsCellMesh.text: The mesh conditions require valid rectangles with negligible overlaps, tested modes contained in resolved modes, and disjoint resolved and eliminated sets. They also impose negation symmetry and the stated axis and degree restrictions.

Breakdown.CertCell.halfPlane.text: The analytic meridian domain is {(r,z):r>0,z>0}. The axis and symmetry plane are excluded from these area integrals.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.CreditPatch.re.text: The credit region is the rectangle from the inner to the outer radius and from z=0 to the specified height.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownSolid.text: The selected solid consists of points of this cell with positive cylindrical radius that belong to no other cell, excluding shared faces from these estimates.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPressu.text: Pressure segments cover all non-axis faces with disjoint interiors, the correct opposite-face coordinates and orthonormal trace tests.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPlaneM.text: Each trace segment on z=0 must have an equal segment and equal test coefficients in the reflected harmonic's coordinates. This condition is stated in one direction.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ActuatorSu.text: Every forcing field equals its admissible compact representation, and the cells cover a square containing all support radii. These conditions also tie the support cutoff to actual spline breakpoints.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.ChartPara.text: The compactified chart uses a length L, a core radius, a small auxiliary parameter ε, and an azimuthal symmetry order κ. Their sign and size conditions are imposed separately.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.IsChartPa.text: The chart requires L>0, a positive core radius, 0<ε<1/8, and κ>0. The final cell certificate strengthens the symmetry-order condition to κ≥3.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.heightRat.text: The normalized height is η=z/|y|, assigned value 0 at y=0. The complete field conditions must supply the required regularity at the origin.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.qOf.text: The polar vanishing factor is 1−η². Away from the origin it vanishes on the rotation axis.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.chartT.text: The compactified radius is σ=|y|/(|y|+L), as in (B.3). It is a spatial coordinate.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.radialVec.text: The radial chart vector is y/|y| away from the origin, with assigned value 0 at y=0. Origin conditions on the full field account for this extension.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.polarVecQ.text: The weighted polar vector is p=(ηy₁/|y|,ηy₂/|y|,−(1−η²)). Its prescribed value at the origin is (0,0,−1); regularity is a condition on the complete field.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.azimVecQ.text: The weighted azimuthal vector is a=(−y₂/|y|,y₁/|y|,0), with value 0 at the origin. It vanishes on the rotation axis.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.TensorMes.text: The spline mesh consists of a radial knot list and a normalized-height knot list. Ordering and endpoint requirements are separate conditions.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.IsTensorM.text: Both knot lists must be strictly increasing, begin at 0, and end at 1. Consequently each direction contains at least one interval.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.cellIndex.text: The selected interval is determined by the number of internal knots at or below the coordinate. At an internal knot, the piece on the right is chosen.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.cellCount.text: The interval count is the number of knots minus one, with result zero for an empty list. A valid mesh has enough ordered endpoints to represent actual intervals.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.text: A spline specifies a complex bivariate polynomial for each pair of interval indices. Values beyond the active mesh range are also part of the representation.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.ev.text: Evaluation first selects the radial and height intervals and then evaluates their polynomial at the given chart coordinates. Agreement and continuity across interfaces require the joining conditions.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.atFirst.text: The operation substitutes a fixed complex value for the first polynomial variable and leaves the second variable unchanged.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.atSecond.text: The operation substitutes a fixed complex value for the second polynomial variable and leaves the first variable unchanged.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.tDeriv.text: The operator takes the specified number of polynomial derivatives in the radial chart variable. Order zero leaves the polynomial unchanged.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.xDeriv.text: The operator takes repeated polynomial derivatives in the normalized-height variable, with the radial variable fixed.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.co.text: Conjugation leaves the spline mesh unchanged and replaces every polynomial coefficient by its complex conjugate.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.Va.text: Every polynomial whose radial left knot is at or beyond the cutoff must vanish, including all height indices. Missing radial knots are assigned value 1, so a cutoff below 1 also requires the corresponding out-of-range pieces to vanish.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.weightPol.text: The endpoint weight is $\sigma^{e_0}(1-\sigma)^{e_1}$ for nonnegative integers $e_0$ and $e_1$. These powers control the origin and far-field behavior.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.radialSca.text: The radial scaling operator is σ(1−σ)∂σ, which equals |y|∂|y| under the compactification. Oscillatory radial phases contribute separate terms.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.heightDer.text: The chart derivative is ∂η at fixed compactified radius σ. It differs from differentiating with respect to the physical height z.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar.text: A scalar weight is specified by upper- and lower-half splines and a nonnegative integer decay exponent. Each half is evaluated using nonnegative normalized height.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar..text: The scalar value is $(1-\sigma)^h$ times the real part of the selected half-chart spline. Points on the symmetry plane use the upper chart.
Reflection exchanges the upper and lower splines and retains the decay exponent.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.SplineJoins.text: The spline conditions require valid knots and equality of polynomial derivatives through the specified order across every internal interface. The interval bounds ensure that each referenced knot lies in the mesh.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsJoinedScal.text: Each half-chart has the required joins, both halves use the same radial knots, and their height derivatives at $\eta=0$ agree with the sign $(-1)^o$ for order $o$.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsConstantCo.text: The cutoff is a positive radial knot, and every active piece below it on either half has one common complex constant. The cutoff and knot-membership requirements hold independently of the universal conditions on pieces.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsFlatAtOrig.text: All active height pieces on both halves have the same value at σ=0. This condition specifies the boundary value alone.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.HasNonnegVal.text: The real part of each half-chart spline must be nonnegative at every point of [0,1]². A finite coefficient test needs a separate argument implying this value inequality.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.text: The auxiliary weight has upper and lower real step tables on a common mesh and an integer power of 1−σ. Negative powers allow growth towards infinity.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsFullMesh.text: The full chart mesh has strictly increasing knots from 0 to 1 in σ and from −1 to 1 in η. The height interval includes both physical halves.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJoinedSp.text: The joining order may differ between σ and η. At every active interface, the required derivatives agree as entire polynomials in the remaining variable.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reflectPol.text: The reflected polynomial is P(σ,−η), with σ unchanged.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reflectSpl.text: Reflection negates and reverses the height knots, reverses the height interval indices, and substitutes −η in each polynomial. The chosen odd parity adds an overall minus sign.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.SplineAgre.text: Spline agreement means equal meshes and equal polynomials on all active rectangles. It places no requirement on unused interval indices.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.KeyAmp.con.text: Amplitude conjugation conjugates all four splines and γ, leaving the origin and far-field exponents unchanged.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.KeyAmp.ref.text: The reflected radial amplitude is A(σ,−η), while the reflected polar, stream, and swirl amplitudes are −B(σ,−η), −S(σ,−η), and −T(σ,−η). The coefficient γ and both exponents remain unchanged.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetDof.text: A jet coordinate specifies either a derivative at a breakpoint or an interior polynomial on one interval. Its index ranges are imposed when selecting the active coordinates.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.text: An interpolation depth D supplies endpoint derivatives of orders 0 through D−1, while the chosen number of interior coordinates supplies additional interval polynomials.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.jetUnit.text: For p<n, the unit-interval Hermite polynomial has p-th derivative 1 at the selected endpoint and the required vanishing derivatives at the opposite endpoint. The formula is zero when p≥n because its coefficient sum is empty.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.nodalLeft.text: The left-endpoint polynomial is obtained by the affine coordinate $(x-a)/(b-a)$ and factor $(b-a)^p$. For $a\ne b$ and $p<n$, where $n$ is the interpolation depth, this preserves the physical $p$-th derivative normalization.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.nodalRight.text: The right-endpoint polynomial uses $(b-x)/(b-a)$ and factor $(a-b)^p$. For $a\ne b$ and $p<n$, where $n$ is the interpolation depth, the reflected coordinate and sign preserve the physical $p$-th derivative normalization.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.bubblePoly.text: The interior polynomial is $[(x-a)(b-x)]^n[x-(a+b)/2]^s$. Its endpoint derivatives of orders $0$ through $n-1$ vanish at both ends.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do.text: A nodal coordinate contributes on its adjacent interval when its derivative order is below the depth. An interior coordinate contributes only on its own interval and within the permitted interior-degree range.
The active coordinates include all endpoint derivatives below the depth at every knot, and the prescribed interior coordinates on every interval.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.re.text: Reflection sends knot k to the opposite knot and interval i to the opposite interval, preserving the derivative or interior-degree index on the active range.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do.text: A reflected $p$-th endpoint derivative has sign $(-1)^p$, and a reflected midpoint polynomial of degree $s$ has sign $(-1)^s$.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetAxis.text: A valid jet axis has strictly increasing knots, the prescribed first and last endpoints, and depth at least one. Every active interval therefore has positive length.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsSymmetri.text: A symmetric height mesh is unchanged by reversing and negating its knot list.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetSpline.text: The tensor-product jet data contain separate radial and height axes and a complex coefficient for each pair of jet coordinates. Evaluation uses their finite active sets.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.embedFirst.text: The radial univariate polynomial becomes a two-variable polynomial independent of η.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.embedSecon.text: The height univariate polynomial becomes a two-variable polynomial independent of σ.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetSpline..text: Each cell polynomial is the sum of products of the active radial and height jet polynomials, weighted by their complex tensor coefficients.
For every radial coordinate and active height coordinate, reflection multiplies its coefficient by the chosen even or odd parity and the derivative-or-interior reflection sign.
A coefficient fixed by conjugate reflection equals the complex conjugate coefficient multiplied by the chosen component parity and the height-coordinate reflection sign.
The value coefficient at the first radial knot is zero for every height coordinate, including height coordinates outside the active set.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.OriginProf.text: The origin function g is specified by a polynomial, a joining point σ_g, and a constant tail. Its normalization and smooth joining are imposed separately.
The polynomial gives g on σ≤σ_g, including the joining point, and the constant tail gives g for σ>σ_g.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsOriginPr.text: The origin function has 0<σ_g≤1 and g(0)=1. When σ_g<1, its value and first two derivatives match the constant tail at the joining point.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.chartCoord.text: For L>0, the compactification σ=|y|/(|y|+L) takes every finite radius into [0,1).

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.chartRadiu.text: The inverse radius is Lσ/(1−σ) on 0≤σ<1. Its assigned value at σ=1 is zero and does not describe a point at infinity.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.phaseSlope.text: The phase derivative factor is 2|y|²f′(|y|²), evaluated using |y|=Lσ/(1−σ).

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.polarFacto.text: The polar factor is 1−η², which vanishes at η=±1.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.axisFactor.text: The stronger axis factor is (1−η²)², used in the nonzero-azimuthal components of (B.7).

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.streamValu.text: The axisymmetric stream amplitude is Ψ=γg(σ)η+S(σ,η). Separating γ identifies the term controlling the gradient at the origin.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reducedCom.text: The formula uses the stream-and-swirl construction (B.8) when ι₁=0 and construction (B.7) otherwise. The latter divides by κι₁, which is nonzero when κ>0 and ι₁≠0.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel.text: The harmonic data must obey conjugation and reflection identities together with the joining orders of (B.7) and (B.8). They also require h₀≥2 in the nonzero-azimuthal case, h≥1 throughout, and the axisymmetric origin-vanishing conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsCompactT.text: The field has the required regularity and symmetry, and its active amplitude splines vanish on pieces starting at or beyond a cutoff below 1. Each such spline has a suitable breakpoint below 1, and every axisymmetric coefficient γ is zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetKeyData.text: The four amplitude splines are specified through endpoint and interior polynomial coefficients, together with γ and the origin and decay exponents.
Each amplitude's jet data are converted into its polynomial spline. The coefficient γ and both exponents are retained unchanged.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.GivenJetDa.text: The finite key set selects harmonic representatives and associates jet data with them. The full model is obtained by conjugation and reflection, with representative consistency imposed separately.
The model converts each representative's jets to amplitude splines and completes their symmetry orbits.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetSpline..text: Every coefficient equals its complex conjugate, so it is real. This requirement applies also to coordinates outside the active interpolation sets.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetClass.text: The radial and height jet axes cover [0,1] and [−1,1], respectively. Their depths are at least one more than the required joining orders.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsGivenJet.text: At most one key from each symmetry orbit may be selected, with the prescribed interpolation depths and origin and decay powers. Keys fixed by conjugation or conjugate reflection must satisfy the corresponding realness and parity conditions.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.mo.text: The radial phase f is replaced by f+af_* while the chart length, symmetry order and origin profile stay fixed.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ph.text: The scalar phase displacement is k·α=Σᵢkᵢαᵢ, as in the moving phase of (B.9).

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.wi.text: Each centre or tangent field can have its own origin profile g while sharing the chart, angular symmetry and radial phase.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.af.text: For fixed chart and phase, the field is W⁰+ΣᵢαᵢWⁱ. Choosing the phase from α introduces additional parameter dependence.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.St.text: The radial cutoff χ is specified by its breakpoints and one polynomial for each interval; joining and cutoff requirements are separate conditions.
The value of χ is the polynomial assigned to the interval containing the argument, with the interval convention also fixing values at breakpoints.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is.text: The cutoff joins through two derivatives, vanishes up to an interior breakpoint σχ and equals one near the endpoint 1.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.st.text: The moving phase is $f_*(s)=\int_0^{\sqrt{s}}\chi(r/(r+L))\,dr/r$. Vanishing of $\chi$ near zero removes the singularity in this integral for valid cutoff data.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr.text: The moving phase integral uses the chosen chart length L and cutoff χ of this profile family.
The proposed radius is rχ=Lσχ/(1−σχ). With valid cutoff data and L>0, the moving phase vanishes inside this radius and parameter dependence there comes only from the affine amplitudes.
At parameter α the radial phase is f+(k·α)f_*; the remaining chart data are unchanged.
Both the centre and tangent fields use the phase selected by α, so the resulting family need not be affine in α outside the fixed-phase core.
A pressure amplitude has separate radial factors at the origin and infinity, an angular vanishing factor and a spline; the exponents are checked by the pressure conditions.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.pr.text: One pressure term is its phase multiplied by $\sigma^{h_0}(1-\sigma)^h(1-\eta^2)^{h'_0}$ and the scalar spline amplitude.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.sh.text: The correction q is the real part of the finite pressure harmonic sum. The pressure gradient used in the residual is subsequently adjusted by −∇(|W|²/2).

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is.text: The pressure coefficients satisfy conjugation, reflection, continuity and decay h≥2, together with the separate axis and origin requirements. For nonzero angular modes, origin regularity permits a positive radial power or exact vanishing of the boundary value.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr.text: The pressure correction combines q⁰+Σᵢαᵢqⁱ after each term has been evaluated with the phase belonging to α.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.pr.text: The centre field uses its own origin profile and the phase fα, so the centre can depend on α even though its harmonic amplitudes are fixed.
Each tangent retains its own amplitudes and origin profile while being evaluated with the common moved phase fα.

Breakdown.CertCell.KnotZero.planeOf.text: A spatial point is sent to $(\sqrt{y_1^2+y_2^2},y_3)$, retaining the sign of its height for the subsequent reflection test.

Breakdown.CertCell.KnotZero.zeroOn.text: The supplied Hessian is set to zero precisely where the meridian coordinates lie in the chosen exceptional set and is retained everywhere else.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.planeNorm.text: The meridian distance is $\sqrt{r^2+z^2}$, the radius used to locate spherical spline seams.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.sphereKnot.text: A radial breakpoint $\sigma$ contributes the sphere $\sqrt{r^2+z^2}=L\sigma/(1-\sigma)$. At $\sigma=1$ the written formula takes the assigned value zero, so this endpoint does not denote an infinite sphere.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.coneKnots.text: A height breakpoint $\eta$ contributes the cone $z=\eta\sqrt{r^2+z^2}$.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.splineKnot.text: The spline's exceptional set is the union of the spherical radial seams and conical height seams.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyKnots.text: Knots from each of the radial, polar, stream and swirl amplitudes are included, even when a particular harmonic uses only part of these data.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeKnots.text: The exceptional set contains the rotation axis, reflection plane, origin, origin-profile joining sphere and every active amplitude seam.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.mirrorKnot.text: The knot set is enlarged to contain its reflection across z=0, making the chosen Hessian representative compatible with this symmetry.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.knotZeroHe.text: The Hessian representative vanishes on the reflection-invariant knot set and equals the harmonic formula off that set; the weak derivative is unchanged when that set has measure zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetA.text: Each axis specifies breakpoints, derivative orders, bubble counts, node scales and bubble normalization factors, all needed to interpret the scaled coefficients.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.symmetricJ.text: The binomial formula fixes the normalization of the symmetric Jacobi polynomial $P_j^{(\alpha,\alpha)}$ used in the bubble basis conversion.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetA.text: The unscaled axis retains the breakpoints, derivative depth and bubble count while omitting the scale and normalization lists.

Node coefficients are multiplied by scale⁻ᵖ, and bubble coefficients by the specified Jacobi and interval-length factors. Missing scales default to 1 and missing bubble normalizations to 0; the formula also assigns values at zero denominators.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasSymmetr.text: The scale list must have one entry per breakpoint and equal its reversal. This condition alone allows zero or negative scales.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetS.text: A tensor spline is specified by two scaled axes and its coefficient array; the associated ordinary Hermite coefficients are obtained by basis conversion.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.complexSl.text: The complex residual is M−diag(δ)−F₊F₊*+F₋F₋*−S, using conjugate transposes in both factor products.
