Every label in the given mode set must have the common class, exact signed memberships, and stated frequency lower bounds. Every inward and outward coupling inequality must hold at every point of the region.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.OffModeCondi.text: The pointwise test data assign a mode set and meridian region to one collection of multiplier lower bounds, stretching charges, and a spatially varying gradient share t.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsOffModeCon.text: The region is a measurable subset of r>0,z>0, the coefficient and charge bounds cover the whole mode-region product, and the charged coefficients pass (B.29) at every point.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeRadius.text: The meridian distance is $\rho=\sqrt{r^2+z^2}=|y|$, including both cylindrical radius and height.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeRayRegi.text: The ray exterior consists of points in r>0,z>0 with ρ greater than the specified threshold. The directional-radius condition makes the threshold constant along each ray.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeSquareE.text: The square exterior is the region r>0,z>0 where r>R or z>R. The exterior estimate separately requires R>0.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsDirectionR.text: The threshold radius is measurable and satisfies 0<R₀≤R(p)≤R₁ everywhere. It is unchanged by every positive dilation, so it depends only on direction away from the origin.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.rayInverseSq.text: The ray-exterior Hardy constant is 1/4+(k−1)₊², combining radial Hardy control and angular derivative control.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.ExteriorCond.text: The exterior data provide the mode and spatial region, coefficient envelopes, stretching charges, a Hardy constant $\Lambda_0$, and the three bounds $f_1^\infty$, $f_0^\infty$, and $f_{01}^\infty$ used in (B.30).

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCo.text: The region is either beyond a positive bounded directional radius, or outside a positive square with zero angular frequency. With one positive $\Lambda_0$, the coefficient bounds and $f_0^\infty/\Lambda_0+f_{01}^\infty/\sqrt{\Lambda_0}\le f_1^\infty$ yield the integrated test.

Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientEntry.text: A finite list of coefficient enclosures is paired with mode sets and spatial regions, which can themselves be infinite. Additional lower coefficients are supplied for resolved and eliminated harmonics.

Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientConditions.text: Every harmonic and every point of the quarter plane must be covered by the appropriate coefficient lower bound, including points outside the mesh. The velocity lower bound is weighted by r²+z².

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.OffModeCover.text: A finite family of regional conditions is supplied, and each cell and integer harmonic selects a finite subfamily to cover its unresolved estimate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsOffModeCov.text: For every non-resolved harmonic, including eliminated harmonics, the selected conditions cover the positive-radius part of the cell, contain that harmonic and dominate the required charges.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ExteriorCove.text: The exterior cover combines finitely many ray-integrated and pointwise regions, with one common charge family and a selection of regions for each harmonic.
The exterior region is taken from whichever ray or pointwise condition is selected.
The selected exterior condition supplies its harmonic set, which may be infinite.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsExteriorCo.text: For each harmonic the selected regions cover the exterior in the quarter plane, lie within it and overlap only on null sets. Every stored condition is valid, and the common charges satisfy the stated measurability and boundedness requirements.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldValu.text: The exterior data supply chart-based bounds for the strain, mean vorticity gradient and oscillatory vorticity gradient.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldCond.text: The chart bounds agree with the exterior charges and control the reference field at every time and angle. The length is positive and common to all harmonics on the exterior.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellHypothesis.text: The cell hypothesis joins seventeen requirements, including the tree, model, trace and support conditions and the fixed values 39/50, 3/50 and 1000. It supplies the first of the fifteen final certificate conditions.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CertificateCla.text: These are the scalar sign, residual, contraction, parameter-inclusion and nontriviality requirements from Section 7. Positivity of the weight and periods is supplied by the other final cell conditions.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CoerciveNumber.text: The supplied numbers bound the multiplier weight, its derivative, the frequency ratio and the total cell error. The same total error is used in both the cell and assembly inequalities.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbers.text: The error from the fixed reference to the centre is separated from the additional change over K; the corresponding gradient bounds use L² and L³ respectively.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbersBo.text: At every time the centre gradient error has an L² bound and the parameter-dependent gradient error has an L³ bound, both using the operator norm. Their weighted sums control the linearization gap and the frozen-form shift.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.PotentialEntri.text: A potential series and chart are supplied for each coefficient index, together with one shared pin representation. Series validity is required only for active adjoint indices.
For every active adjoint, the potential and pin fields must equal the validated represented fields. Agreement of the shared pin matrix with the certificate holds for the full family.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ReductionEntri.text: The reduction data supply the profile, pressure, adjoints, offsets, shifts and potentials used to obtain the Section 7 certificate; all conditions use these same choices.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCond.text: All fifteen conditions must hold for the same seven collections of data. They give a conditional route from those data to the certificate and do not provide a particular numerical certificate.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpa.text: If all fifteen cell conditions hold, every positive viscosity admits smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data on ℝ³ with no global smooth bounded-energy solution. The readable file states this implication; its proof belongs to the separate proof library.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnTor.text: If all fifteen cell conditions hold, every positive viscosity admits smooth periodic divergence-free data with no global smooth solution preserving the velocity periodicity, allowing any smooth pressure. The readable file states the implication, whose proof is supplied separately.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.breakdownOnSpa.text: One set of data satisfying all fifteen cell conditions yields both the whole-space and periodic nonexistence conclusions. This implication remains conditional on the data satisfying those conditions.

The conclusion follows conditionally from one shared choice of all seven data collections satisfying the fifteen certificate conditions. The sentence asserts this implication and supplies no particular numerical certificate.

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).
